content: Digital Forensics: FAT/exFAT Cluster Carving, CHKDSK Anomaly Analysis & 44 GB Network Storage Reclamation Completed Project Digital Forensics · File Carving · FAT32/exFAT Clusters · EXIF Reconstruction · Storage Reclamation · Antigravity AI · November 21, 2026 📸 View Real Live Terminal Workbench Capture in the Visual Gallery (#fat-cluster-carving-storage-reclamation) → 44 GB Corrupt FOUND.000 (.CHK) Cluster Chains → Magic Byte Header Triage (SOI / EOI Markers) → Automated Python/Pillow Signature Carving → EXIF Datetime & Camera Hardware Reconstruction → 135 Salvaged Photos & 42 GB Net Space Reclaimed 🔬 Forensic Carving & Cluster Deconstruction Pipeline 44 GB Corrupt FAT Chains → Magic Byte Bounding → EXIF Timestamp Reconstruction → 42+ GB Reclaimed Digital Forensics • Python / Pillow 1. Corrupt Cluster Dump /FOUND.000 (44 GB) • 368 Orphaned .CHK Files • Severed FAT Directory Tables • Up to 2.84 GB / file (Glued) CRITICAL CAPACITY 93% Used • Only 33 GB Free 2. Magic Byte Triage Header Signature Scan JPEG: 0xFFD8FF • PNG: 0x89504E → 135 Valid Media Candidates Non-Media Filter 233 Partial Blobs (Wii ISOs/Videos) Binary Stream Boundary Analysis 3. Pillow Carve & EXIF True EOF Slicing Trim at ÿÙ • Strip Garbage Pillow img.verify() Strict Bitmap Integrity Check Catch Faulty Streams In-Memory EXIF Metadata Mining Tags 0x9003 / 0x0132 • Make & Model Pixel 9, Pixel 7, Note 10+, S21, iPhone 11 4. Reclaimed Storage 135 Salvaged Photos 1.39 GB Total Payload Clean Canonical Naming YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_cam.jpg +42 GB RECLAIMED 33 GB → 75 GB Free Space 84% Healthy Drive Capacity During an automated storage and content audit of an Intel NUC's 500 GB network-attached USB drive ( ONEFIVE ), disk capacity was discovered sitting at a precarious 93% utilization (only 33 GB available), threatening upcoming iCloud photo synchronizations. Diagnostic exploration identified a massive 44 GB legacy directory at /media/onefive/FOUND.000 holding 368 orphaned FILExxxx.CHK artifacts. While frequently assumed to be empty zero-byte placeholders, binary analysis revealed non-empty data clusters generated by Windows CHKDSK on July 11, 2026 following an ungraceful hardware disconnect. Rather than blindly purging the folder, we treated it as a real-world digital forensics laboratory exercise to audit, carve, and salvage unbacked-up family media before reclaiming disk capacity. 1. Forensic Triage & Cluster Concatenation Anomalies Zero-Byte Hypothesis Refutation: Statistical analysis across all 368 files proved that exactly zero files were empty. File sizes ranged from 128 KB (the filesystem's native cluster allocation block) up to 2.84 GB, with 20 distinct files exceeding 1.0 GB and 31 exceeding 100 MB. Cluster Chain Anomaly: Inspecting raw file headers via magic bytes revealed an interesting NTFS/FAT recovery phenomenon: multiple multi-gigabyte files started with valid JPEG Start of Image ( 0xFFD8FF ) headers from modern mobile devices (Google Pixel 9, Samsung Galaxy S21 Ultra, Galaxy Note 10+ 5G). Because chkdsk lost directory allocation records and file length markers during the crash, it bundled thousands of adjacent, unallocated sectors onto the initial photo cluster, bloating single photos into 2.3 GB to 2.8 GB Frankenstein files. Data Classification: Header classification revealed 130 files starting with JPEG signatures, 5 files with PNG signatures, and ~233 raw binary blobs (truncated ISO disc images and video streams from interrupted write operations). 2. Automated Signature Carving & Metadata Reconstruction To recover valid media without dragging along tens of gigabytes of appended garbage sectors, we developed an automated forensic carving script in Python using Pillow and low-level byte streaming: SOI to EOI Boundary Trimming: For each JPEG artifact, the script identified the primary SOI marker ( ÿØÿ ), isolated the true End of Image boundary ( ÿÙ ), and cleanly sliced the byte array, discarding unreferenced trailing sectors. For PNGs, it bounded chunks by the IEND marker and validated the 4-byte CRC. Bitmap Integrity Verification: Sliced payloads were loaded into memory via Image.open(io.BytesIO(...)) and validated with img.verify() , ensuring corrupt headers or unreadable streams were safely caught without halting the batch. EXIF Reconstruction & Canonical Renaming: Re-parsed the validated streams to extract embedded TIFF EXIF tags ( 0x9003 / 0x0132 capture timestamps, 0x010f Make, and 0x0110 Model). The carver programmatically renamed each recovered asset according to its authentic capture timeline and originating device (e.g., 20211210201438_FILE0041_Google_Pixel_3a.jpg , 20240127134649_FILE0128_samsung_SM-G998U1.jpg , and 20250106174443_FILE0359_Google_Pixel_9.jpg ). 3. Forensic Findings, Archival & Storage Reclamation 135 Intact Images Recovered: The carving pipeline extracted 135 verified, undamaged photographs and graphics totaling 1.39 GB—condensing 44 GB of bloated cluster chains down to their true payload size with zero corruption. Deduplication Cross-Check: Cross-checking recovered timestamps against the active Google Photos archive revealed that while many photos were redundant clusters from past syncs, several historical Pixel 3a photos from 2021 and orphaned family captures were safely rescued. Storage Headroom Restored: All 135 images were safely archived into /media/onefive/salvaged_photos/ . With all recoverable digital evidence secured, /media/onefive/FOUND.000 was cleanly purged. Available storage on ONEFIVE jumped from 33 GB (93% full) to 75 GB (84% full) —reclaiming over 42 GB of free space and ensuring ample headroom for incoming iCloud photo streams. AI collaboration credit: Andrew identified the storage constraint on ONEFIVE, approved the forensic triage strategy, and guided recovery objectives as practical coursework for his digital forensics studies. Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) performed remote binary triage over SSH, engineered and executed the automated Python carving and EXIF extraction pipeline, safely reclaimed 42+ GB of network storage, and authored this case study. content: Heterogeneous 9-Node Hardware Fleet Hub, Homelab Incident Simulator & AI Bias Audit Lab: E-Waste Reclamation, ITAM Telemetry & Algorithmic Auditing Completed Project Hardware Salvage · ITAM / GLPI · Chaos Engineering · Algorithmic Fairness · E-Waste ROI · Antigravity AI · November 21, 2026 Heterogeneous 9-Node Salvaged Homelab Fleet & 3-Tier Rack → 3D-Ready SVG Workbench Topology (Bottom-Shelf USB Host Tethering) → Hardware Longevity & Salvage ROI Calculator ($11,850+ Reclaimed) → Interactive Homelab Incident Response & Chaos Simulator → Algorithmic Bias & Fairness Audit Lab (Real-World Analogies & EEOC 80% Rule) Across homelab engineering, enterprise IT administration, and machine learning, true technical expertise does not come from observing sanitized environments—it is forged through direct ownership, unexpected system dependencies, thermal troubleshooting, and resolving failures under pressure. In a deep pair programming collaboration with Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) , I architected, engineered, and deployed three standalone production-grade laboratories directly into this portfolio: the Hardware Fleet & Salvage Architecture Hub , the Homelab Incident Response & Chaos Simulator , and the AI Bias & Algorithmic Fairness Audit Lab . Interactive 3D Digital Twin, 4-Tier Rack Kinematics & Sub-Component Telemetry To eliminate physical abstraction and provide true visual grounding for remote administration, I engineered an interactive 3D WebGL digital twin of my homelab workbench built on Three.js (r128) and OrbitControls. Photogrammetrically aligned to the physical room layout, the model features: 4-Tier Freestanding Rack Architecture: Accurately models physical vertical spacing across all four tiers where the upright poles terminate flush with the topmost shelf (zero extension beyond the desk tier): Shelf 1 (Top) anchors the primary administrative FREEHPGAMER workstation on a wire mesh riser, ONEFIVE Sabrent external storage enclosure, and the modular snap-cube tower with the headless Alpine NUC and Adafruit Bluefruit status beacon; Shelf 2 (Upper-Middle) houses the Linux Mint 21 HP Workhorse laptop and 3.5" USB floppy drive reader; Shelf 3 (Lower-Middle) provides a dedicated horizontal bay for HOMEDELL 2 (Dell Inspiron running Slax in RAM) topped by the navy blue USB-C multiport hub; and Shelf 4 (Bottom) holds the Debian Mid-2011 Mac, bare-board Lenovo Yoga 2 11 rig, 5V USB blower fan, and tethered Samsung Galaxy S4 Mini miner. Solid Filled-In Side Panels & Flush Upright Geometry: Both the main 4-tier rack and secondary side unit vertical posts terminate flush with their respective topmost shelves (y = 16.2 on main rack, y = 6.85 on compact side shelf). Accurately reflecting the real-world workbench build, the main rack features solid filled-in wooden side panels on both the left (x = -10.4) and right (x = 10.4) flanks, leaving the front and rear open for direct hardware access and airflow. The compact secondary shelf sits immediately to the right with its rear-left post at x = 11.4, z = 2.8, creating a clean L-shaped corner footprint. Shelf 1 Storage Architecture (Rotated ONEFIVE & Samsung 870 EVO SSD): Positioned directly in front of the Intel NUC (z = 1.6) sits the ONEFIVE Sabrent USB 3.0 Enclosure , rotated 90 degrees so its cyan LED status indicator aligns with the right edge of the NUC (x = 6.9) and wired directly to the NUC's rear USB 3.0 bus. Resting directly on top of the ONEFIVE enclosure is a dedicated Samsung 870 EVO 500GB 2.5" SSD (HL-STOR-02-EVO870) complete with signature red accent square badge, connected via USB 3.0 to FREEHPGAMER to store macOS VirtualBox VM images and academic cloning project templates. Non-Clipping Ethernet Routing, Floppy USB Link & Slower Bluefruit Cycling: High-visibility yellow Cat6 cables originate from the 8-port switch on the secondary shelf (y = 4.85) and enter the main rack through the open front corner (z = 3.2 to 3.5), routing strictly above wooden shelf planks without intersecting upright posts. On Shelf 2, the Ethernet cable routes cleanly in front of the floppy drive directly into the HP Laptop 15's USB-C adapter, while a separate black USB cable connects the floppy drive to the laptop's left port. The Adafruit Bluefruit status beacon's NeoPixel rotating LED array has been tuned to a slower, authentic color-cycling cadence. Architectural Wall Ledge, Landscape Miners & Duplex AC Wall Charging Station: Behind and strictly to the left of the freestanding rack sits the natural built-in wall ledge at y=9.3. Resting on the ledge on desktop kickstands in 90-degree landscape orientation are the Samsung Galaxy Player (YP-GI1) and Apple iPod Touch 1G miners. Mounted on the wall behind the leftmost shelf edge is a Duplex AC Wall Outlet equipped with dual dedicated USB charger bricks: an upper Apple 5W USB adapter supplying 30-pin power to the iPod Touch, and a lower black USB adapter powering the Galaxy Player. Shelf 4 Hardware Realism (Vertical Yoga PCB, Overhead Blower Fan & S4 Mini): The Lenovo Yoga 2 Pro motherboard is mounted vertically on edge in the Y-Z plane, presenting an ultra-thin profile (0.08 units) when viewed head-on and exposing its full green PCB layout, Intel CPU die, and copper heatpipe upon rotating 90 degrees. Active cooling is delivered by an authentic 5V Centrifugal Blower Fan mounted overhead directly above the Yoga board, with its exhaust duct angled downward (-Y) and outward (+Z) to blow down onto the PCB and outward across the copper heatsink. To the left of the Yoga sits the Samsung Galaxy S4 Mini with its rear cover removed, exposing its lithium-ion battery cell, terminal contacts, and camera module. Mathematical CAD Ray Zooming (Zero Gimbal Spin), Camera Presets & Hover Illumination: Features mathematically coupled CAD ray zooming that translates both camera position and target together along the cursor ray, eliminating gimbal singularity and violent spinning even when viewing directly from above. Includes state-tracked cursor ergonomics (grabbing fist, open hand, finger pointer), a multi-tier camera dropdown selector, and real-time hover illumination rendering live GLPI asset telemetry. Heterogeneous Hardware Fleet & Physical Shelving Architecture Rather than letting aging or damaged computers end up in municipal landfills, my homelab operates as a living testbed for circular hardware lifecycle engineering across an integrated 4-tier rack, compact secondary network shelf, and architectural wall ledge. The Hardware Fleet & Salvage Hub documents the exact hardware specifications, physical telemetry, and continuous 24/7 production workloads across all fleet tiers: Shelf 1 (Top Shelf · Primary Compute & Virtualization): Anchors FREEHPGAMER from Fishbeck (Windows 11 workstation on wire riser for Folding@home and hypervisor labs), the Headless Intel NUC Core Backbone (Alpine Linux musl running BOINC research simulations, AdGuard Home DNS sinkhole, and Tailscale WireGuard mesh), the Adafruit Circuit Playground Bluefruit status beacon, the rotated ONEFIVE Sabrent USB 3.0 Enclosure linked to the NUC, and a dedicated Samsung 870 EVO 500GB SSD storing macOS VirtualBox VM images and academic cloning templates. Shelf 2 (Upper-Middle Shelf · Generative AI & Legacy Media): Houses the HP Laptop 15 Workhorse (Linux Mint 21 executing Realistic Vision 5.1 batch image diffusion queues and Rclone Google Drive cloud sync, connected via a Gigabit Ethernet-to-USB-C adapter) and the vintage 3.5" USB Floppy Drive Reader paired with an optical media digitization hub wired directly into the laptop via USB. Shelf 3 (Lower-Middle Shelf · Pure RAM Compute): Features HOMEDELL 2 (Dell Inspiron 3668) positioned horizontally on its dedicated shelf tier, booting 100% into RAM off a custom Slax Linux live USB with persistence overlay (zero spinning disk dependency) and topped by the navy blue USB-C multiport hub with dual 2.4 GHz nano-receivers. Shelf 4 (Bottom Shelf · Open Testbench & Mobile Mining): Houses the Debian Mid-2011 Mac (aluminum unibody with battery proactively removed for 24/7 desk safety, serving as host compute and compile node), the Lenovo Yoga 2 Pro Bare-Board Rig (motherboard mounted vertically on edge in the Y-Z plane for maximum thermal dissipation, wired via Gigabit Ethernet-to-USB-A adapter), an authentic 5V Centrifugal Blower Fan mounted overhead directly above the board delivering forced downward and outward cooling, and the Samsung Galaxy S4 Mini (SCH-I435) to the left of the Yoga running 24/7 Duino-Coin web worker threads with its back cover off and battery exposed. Secondary Shelf Unit (Right Flank · Network Infrastructure & Print): Houses the 8-Port Gigabit Managed Switch Backbone on the middle tier (y = 4.2) anchoring all yellow Cat6 interconnects, and an active domestic HP Network Multifunction Printer on the bottom tier (y = 1.6) providing CUPS document spooling over local Wi-Fi. Architectural Wall Ledge (Left Flank · Dedicated Mobile Miners): Houses the Samsung Galaxy Player (YP-GI1) and Apple iPod Touch 1G miners propped in 90-degree landscape orientation at a ~70° angle on kickstands, powered 24/7 by a dedicated Duplex AC Wall Outlet with dual USB charging adapters. 3D-Ready Interactive Topology, GLPI ITAM & Salvage ROI Calculator To provide full transparency into how these systems interact, the fleet hub incorporates three core technical systems: Interactive 3D-Ready Shelf Schematic: A responsive SVG/canvas workbench viewport mapping physical node placement across the three tiers: Physical Shelves & Workbench Layout , Network Mesh & Active Ports , Thermal Dissipation & Power Profiling , and GLPI Inventory Mode . Shows physical USB host tethering between the 2011 Mac and S4 Mini, as well as wall-powered mobile miners, with an open integration slot for a custom photogrammetry 3D model (GLTF) or workbench capture. GLPI IT Asset Management (ITAM) Integration: Models an enterprise IT asset lifecycle schema tracking asset tags (e.g. HL-NODE-06-NUC-CORE , HL-NODE-01-S4MINI , HL-NODE-08-GALPLAYER ), depreciation amortizations, physical interfaces, assigned service daemons, and last maintenance verification dates. To transform this documentation archive into an engaging, living exploratory experience—accessible to anyone on the public web without requiring private Tailscale tunnels or specialized backend proxies—I collaborated with Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) to engineer and deploy an interactive 3D WebGL knowledge map and project constellation accessible under the Systems & Stats navigation menu. 3D Force-Directed Constellation Engine & Spatial Clustering We built the visualization engine upon Three.js and 3d-force-graph , leveraging hardware-accelerated WebGL to render an interactive celestial node system running smoothly at 60 frames per second on both mobile touchscreens and desktop viewports: Hierarchical Galactic Clustering: The universe is anchored by six major domain galaxy hubs ( AI & Agentic Systems , Homelab & Networking , Digital Forensics & Recovery , Embedded Hardware & Mining , Audio/Video & Creative , and Enterprise IT & Automation ). Physics repulsion forces cluster related projects naturally in 3D space around their domain anchors. Dynamic Project Nodes & Status Badges: Each project exists as an interactive celestial body sized by scope and colored by operational status (Completed Project 🟢 vs. In Progress 🟡), rendering high-resolution billboard sprite labels that face the camera dynamically during rotation. Satellite Task Orbiters: Individual milestones, architectural subsystems, and active tasks orbit parent projects as satellite sub-nodes, allowing visitors to inspect granular progress and sub-features at a glance. Cross-Project Technology Bridges: Shared technologies (such as Alpine Linux , Tailscale , FastAPI , Python , and Docker ) act as gravitational bridges, illuminating shared architectural patterns across homelab, cloud, and edge systems. Zero-Tailscale Client-Side Static Architecture A critical architectural priority was ensuring that any public visitor on the open internet can seamlessly interact with the 3D map without encountering network authentication walls, Tailscale mesh requirements, or proxy bottlenecks: Automated Graph Extraction Pipeline: Developed an automated Python builder ( scripts/build-knowledge-graph.py ) that extracts semantic metadata, technological tags, sub-tasks, and relationships directly from projects.html and compiles a static, optimized payload at data/knowledge-map.json . Client-Side WebGL Rendering: The entire force simulation, collision detection, and camera choreography execute directly inside the client's web browser. The application requires zero active backend runtime, ensuring instant sub-second page loads globally via Cloudflare / GitHub Pages CDN. Cinematic Flight Navigation, Search Indexing & Telemetry HUD To deliver an intuitive and fluid user experience, the 3D map features an ambient glassmorphism Heads-Up Display (HUD): Smooth Camera Fly-To Interpolation: Clicking any project or domain node activates a smooth cinematic camera flight that glides the viewport directly toward the target coordinate while preserving orbit angles. Real-Time Search & Auto-Focus: An integrated search bar filters nodes dynamically as the user types, highlighting matches in the 3D space and enabling instant keyboard flight to any project or task. Slide-Out Telemetry Drawer: Selecting any node opens a responsive frosted-glass side panel presenting project metadata, status chips, sub-task breakdowns, technology tags, and a direct deep link to the complete writeup in projects.html . Display Mode & Rotation Controls: Visitors can toggle continuous auto-orbit rotation, reset camera perspectives, switch between 3D spherical constellation and 2D planar force layouts, or filter the graph by specific domains and statuses. Interaction Ergonomics: Smooth Cubic Hover Transitions, Boundary Unsticking & Single-Session Orbit Halting During live cross-device user testing, we identified subtle interaction friction when navigating dense node clusters and interacting with modal HUD overlays. Collaborating with Antigravity AI , we engineered targeted architectural refinements across the interaction pipeline: Boundary-Aware Hover Unsticking: When navigating from a hovered node directly into the frosted-glass telemetry drawer or HUD controls, the 3D canvas previously stopped receiving native pointermove raycast events, leaving the previously hovered node persistently stuck in a highlighted state. We implemented global boundary listeners across #telemetry-drawer , the HUD toolbars, and the canvas container ( mouseleave and mouseenter ) that immediately trigger clearHoverState() , ensuring nodes cleanly deselect the instant the cursor transitions onto UI overlays. Smooth Cubic Easing Transitions: Previously, hovering or unhovering nodes caused instantaneous binary alpha toggling, causing the constellation to abruptly pop into and out of high contrast in a single frame. We implemented a requestAnimationFrame easing tween governed by a cubic ease-out curve ( 1 - Math.pow(1 - p, 3) ) over a calibrated 260ms window. Non-connected nodes smoothly fade their alpha from 1.0 down to 0.18 upon hover, and gently breathe back up to full brightness upon cursor departure without visual jitter. Single-Session Orbit Halting: To eliminate initial render stutter, we removed conflicting animation tweens during physics warmup ( warmupTicks(35) ), stabilizing the initial camera at { x: 0, y: 25, z: 420 } . Auto-rotation starts immediately on page load via native Three.js OrbitControls , but the instant the user begins dragging, scrolling/zooming, panning, or selecting nodes, auto-rotation halts permanently for the duration of the session, preventing the camera from snapping back or wrestling with user navigation until the page is refreshed. content: HP Laptop 15 (Linux Mint) Realistic Vision 5.1 Wallpaper Generator: Interface Simplification, Fixed 1080p LCM Inference, Continuous Ad Infinitum Loop & Persistent Rclone Google Drive Cloud Sync Completed Project Linux Mint 22.3 · Realistic Vision V5.1 · stable-diffusion.cpp · LCM LoRA · Fixed 1080p · Ad Infinitum Inference · Python Reverse Proxy · Rclone FUSE Mount · Google Drive OAuth2 · Systemd User Service · Antigravity AI · November 20, 2026 HP Laptop Desktop UI / Web Browser (http://127.0.0.1:7865) → Python Launcher & Reverse Proxy (Port 7865) → stable-diffusion.cpp Engine (Internal Port 7866 / CPU Backend) → Continuous Ad Infinitum Loop (1920×1080, LCM 6 Steps, CFG 1.0, VAE Tiling) → Server-Side Persistence (/api/save) → Persistent Rclone FUSE Mount (~/GoogleDrive/AI-Wallpapers) → Google Drive (avanek2005@gmail.com) On my primary HP laptop ( avanek-hp-laptop-15-db0xxx , AMD Ryzen 3 2200U with Radeon Vega Mobile Graphics, 16 GB RAM running Linux Mint 22.3), I maintain a local desktop shortcut for Realistic Vision 5.1 that launches a local C++ inference backend ( stable-diffusion.cpp ). While the local CPU model was capable of generating photorealistic imagery, the default setup suffered from high operational friction: it loaded a heavy 128 KB monolithic Vue web interface cluttered with multi-panel LoRA tables, multi-modal image dropzones (Init image, Mask, ControlNet, Ref images), VAE tiling parameter inputs, and cache toggles, as well as an AnimateDiff v3 motion module that consumed 836 MB of memory even for static renders. Furthermore, generation was capped to manual single-run requests, image resolution was unfixed, and newly rendered wallpapers required clicking manual browser "Download" buttons on every single image before closing the terminal, risking output loss on exit. Collaborating with Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) , we overhauled the application end-to-end into an autonomous, friction-free wallpaper synthesis engine: locked permanently to 1920×1080 Full HD, running fast Latent Consistency Model (LCM) inference in 6 steps, rendering continuously in an unattended infinite loop ( cooking ad infinitum ), and streaming every finished render directly to persistent cloud storage on Google Drive under avanek2005@gmail.com . Minimalist Single-View Web UI & Fixed 1080p Standard To eliminate interface clutter and streamline the generation workflow, we completely redesigned and replaced the monolithic frontend ( ui.html ) with a clean, responsive dark-mode interface: Eradication of UI Clutter: Completely stripped away extraneous UI controls including manual LoRA configuration tables, multi-modal image inputs (Init image, Mask, ControlNet, Ref images), VAE tiling toggles, DiT/UNET cache selectors, and AnimateDiff video generation tabs. Unhooked the 836 MB video motion module from the launcher, reclaiming substantial system memory for inference. Fixed 1920×1080 Geometry: Eliminated manual resolution dropdowns and sliders. Generation dimensions are locked permanently to 1920×1080 (Full HD) across both frontend API payloads and the backend engine invocation ( -W 1920 -H 1080 ). Streamlined Controls: Reduced the interactive footprint to a clean prompt description textarea paired with a high-contrast “▶ Start Generating” button that dynamically transforms into a pulsing “⏹ Stop Generation” interrupt button while rendering. Live Telemetry & Showcase Viewport: Integrated a 16:9 full-viewport output preview frame, real-time step and session elapsed timers, cumulative cooked-image counter, active target destination indicator, and a session render history strip with an interactive lightbox modal for full-resolution review. Fast LCM Inference & Autonomous Continuous Loop ( Ad Infinitum ) On CPU hardware, standard diffusion samplers (such as DPM++ 2M / Karras at 20 steps) take 40+ minutes per image. We re-engineered the pipeline around speed and autonomy: Fast LCM Acceleration: Configured the Latent Consistency Model speed adapter ( lcm.safetensors , multiplier 1.0) with 6 sampling steps, CFG scale 1.0, and the LCM sampler/scheduler. VAE tiling ( --vae-tiling ) is permanently enforced in the backend to ensure stable 1080p latent decoding within CPU memory bounds without UI intervention. Continuous Unattended Synthesis Loop: Transformed manual single-image generation into an automated, unattended infinite generation loop ( while (isGenerating) ). The engine automatically synthesizes wallpaper after wallpaper with dynamic randomized seeds ( seed: -1 ), polling engine status every 800ms. Responsive Halting Engine: Programmed a non-blocking interrupt mechanism: clicking “Stop Generation” immediately transmits an engine cancellation request ( POST /sdcpp/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel ) and halts the loop cleanly without process deadlock, orphaned locks, or corrupted outputs. Dual-Port Reverse Proxy & Server-Side Auto-Save Persistence Modern browser sandboxes restrict automated file downloads, triggering intrusive multi-file security prompts or saving files to random default browser directories. We solved this at the architecture layer: Python Reverse Proxy Architecture ( launch.py ): Restructured the application launcher into a dual-tiered architecture. The native stable-diffusion.cpp binary ( sd-server ) is isolated on internal loopback port 7866 , while a multi-threaded Python HTTP proxy server listens on public port 7865 , serving ui.html , handling configuration discovery ( /api/config ), and proxying engine calls. Automated /api/save Persistence Endpoint: As each 1080p wallpaper finishes in memory, the client immediately POSTs the decoded base64 PNG data to /api/save . The Python backend writes the binary directly to disk using standardized timestamps and seed metadata ( rv1080p_YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS_s<seed>.png ), logging file path and byte telemetry directly to the terminal. Multi-Tier Storage Failover: Engineered a resilient storage resolver ( resolve_output_dir() ) prioritizing: (1) Primary Google Drive cloud storage ( ~/GoogleDrive/AI-Wallpapers ), (2) Secondary central network Samba automount ( /mnt/ONEFIVE/_TEMP/Image_Gen_Runz ), and (3) Tertiary local disk fallback ( ROOT/outputs ). Persistent Rclone Cloud Mount & Google Drive Shortcut Traversal To ensure newly synthesized wallpapers are immediately accessible across all laptops, phones, and workstations without manual network copies, we integrated persistent cloud storage under my personal account: Remote Credential Migration & Quota Audit: Retired the legacy university cloud mount ( rclone-gdrive.service referencing vaneka@mail.gvsu.edu ). Imported and validated the authenticated OAuth2 token for the avanek2005 Google Drive remote in ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf , verifying access to my 5.0 TiB storage quota (146.9 GiB used) and discovering the dedicated AI-Wallpapers destination folder. Transparent Cross-Account Shortcut Resolution: In Google Drive, AI-Wallpapers is configured as a cross-account shortcut pointer ( application/vnd.google-apps.shortcut ). Rclone's FUSE VFS layer transparently traverses the shortcut pointer, exposing the remote folder as a standard writable Linux directory. Systemd User Service Modernization: Deployed and enabled ~/.config/systemd/user/rclone-google-drive.service with write-back caching ( --vfs-cache-mode writes --vfs-cache-max-age 24h --dir-cache-time 5m --drive-pacer-min-sleep 10ms ) registered on default.target for persistent boot mounting to ~/GoogleDrive . Validated full write, read, and deletion capabilities with live FUSE filesystem probes. AI collaboration credit: Andrew Van Ek defined the continuous infinite generation loop, locked 1080p resolution, and interface simplification requirements, designated the avanek2005@gmail.com Google Drive cloud target, and tested and validated live unattended wallpaper synthesis. Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) inspected the existing HP laptop workspace, authored the streamlined dark-mode ui.html , re-engineered launch.py into a dual-port reverse proxy with automated server-side base64 persistence, eliminated memory overhead by decoupling the AnimateDiff module, configured and deployed the persistent systemd Rclone user mount for avanek2005@gmail.com , validated FUSE shortcut traversal, resolved multi-tier storage failover, and authored this case study. content: Google Cloud VM (Debian 12) Realistic Vision V6 Wallpaper Generator: Continuous Ad Infinitum Inference, Minimalist 1080p Web UI & Zero-Prompt Rclone Google Drive Sync Completed Project Google Cloud Platform (GCP) · Debian 12 · Realistic Vision V6 · stable-diffusion.cpp · Rclone · Google Drive OAuth2 · Headless Web Architecture · Ad Infinitum Inference · November 19, 2026 GCP VM Desktop UI / Web Browser (http://127.0.0.1:1234) → Python Launcher & Micro-Server (Port 1234) → stable-diffusion.cpp Engine (Realistic Vision V6 / CPU Port) → Continuous Ad Infinitum Loop (1920×1080, DPM++ 2M, Karras) → Local Storage (~/AI-Wallpapers) → Rclone Background Queue (--no-traverse) → Google Drive (gdrive:AI-Wallpapers) On my 8-vCPU Google Cloud Compute Engine VM ( fah-cpu-8 , c2-standard-8 in us-central1-c running Debian 12 with an XFCE desktop accessible over Tailscale VNC), I had an existing "Local Photo" desktop shortcut running a heavy upstream stable-diffusion.cpp WebUI. While functional, it suffered from friction: generating images required navigating complex sub-panels and sliders, resolutions varied, batch generation was capped, users had to click manual browser "Download" buttons on every single image before closing the terminal, and output images were discarded on exit if not saved manually. Collaborating with Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) , we overhauled the entire architecture into an unattended, continuous 1080p wallpaper generation pipeline that automatically saves renders locally and streams them directly into my 5.0 TiB Google Drive storage under avanek2005@gmail.com . Minimalist 1080p Web UI & Photorealistic Parameter Locking We replaced the monolithic upstream Vue WebUI with an ultra-clean, dark-themed responsive interface designed for distraction-free prompting: Locked 1920×1080 Full HD Geometry: Completely eliminated dimension sliders and aspect ratio inputs. Generation geometry is permanently hardcoded to 1920×1080 Full HD across both frontend payloads and the C++ engine invocation ( -W 1920 -H 1080 ). Automated Negative Prompt & Sampler Injection: Pre-configured the engine with Realistic Vision V6 photorealism negative prompts (eradicating painting, cartoon, 3D render, blur, and artifacts) alongside optimal inference settings (20 sampling steps, CFG scale 5.0, DPM++ 2M sampler, and Karras sigma scheduler). Live 16:9 Viewport & Session Lightbox: Built a 16:9 presentation container that displays the active wallpaper with live step/elapsed timers, dynamic generation overlays, and an interactive horizontal session gallery strip allowing instant full-resolution inspection. Continuous Unattended Generation Loop ( Ad Infinitum ) To eliminate manual batch size limits and browser download popups, we re-architected the Python launcher service ( /home/fold/.local/bin/local-photo ): Autonomous Multi-Threaded Generator: Clicking "Start Continuous Generation" launches an unattended background worker loop. Each iteration generates a cryptographically random seed ( random.randint(1, 2147483647) ), submits the job to the local stable-diffusion.cpp HTTP engine, polls status, decodes the rendered base64 PNG directly from inference memory, and writes it to disk ( ~/AI-Wallpapers/rv1080p_YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS_s<seed>.png ). Ad Infinitum Persistence: The generator immediately cycles to the next image without stopping, continuing forever until explicitly halted. Because generation runs in a backend daemon thread rather than frontend JavaScript timers, background browser tab throttling cannot stall or drop active rendering passes. Responsive Interrupt Engine: Clicking "Stop Generation" seamlessly signals the worker, transmits a non-blocking cancellation request to the engine ( /sdcpp/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel ), and cleanly halts the loop without file corruption or deadlocks. Rclone Google Drive Deployment & Headless Loopback OAuth Triage To automatically sync generated wallpapers to cloud storage without manual intervention, we integrated Rclone with Google Drive for avanek2005@gmail.com : Port 53682 Connection Refusal Diagnosis: During initial configuration, executing rclone config reconnect resulted in an immediate browser error ( Firefox can't connect to 127.0.0.1:53682 ). Investigating the execution lifecycle revealed that standard interactive reconnection commands paused waiting for an unprompted y/n (auto config) input on stdin; when executed headless or via desktop shortcuts, EOF was triggered, causing Rclone to terminate before the local HTTP callback listener could bind to port 53682. Dedicated Zero-Prompt OAuth Wrapper ( setup-rclone-gdrive ): Engineered a Python setup utility that directly launches rclone authorize "drive" . This bypasses all interactive stdin prompts, immediately binds port 53682, automatically launches Firefox to Google's OAuth consent screen on the VM desktop ( DISPLAY=:0.0 ), captures the returned JSON token upon user approval, and safely commits it into ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf . Directory Traversal Optimization ( --no-traverse ) & Background Sync My Google Drive account hosts thousands of existing wallpapers within the target AI-Wallpapers shortcut folder: Eliminating API Traversal Latency: In standard mode, Rclone performs full remote directory listings prior to uploading. With thousands of files in AI-Wallpapers , scanning the remote directory caused 15–20 second latency penalties per file. We implemented the --no-traverse flag in the background synchronization worker ( rclone copy --no-traverse file.png gdrive:AI-Wallpapers/ ), allowing each finished wallpaper to stream to Google Drive within sub-second intervals. Local Desktop Symlink Integration: Symlinked ~/AI-Wallpapers directly to ~/Desktop/AI-Wallpapers , allowing local file browsing and cloud synchronization to happen simultaneously. An in-memory cache check verifies token validity in sub-milliseconds, displaying a real-time green cloud synchronization indicator in the Web UI header. Process Supervision & Safe RAM Cleanup Because the Google Cloud VM operates under strict RAM constraints, lingering background inference servers can exhaust memory: Parent Death Signaling: Configured prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM) so that if the parent terminal session terminates, all child C++ inference processes immediately terminate. Signal Interception & Mutex Locking: Bound SIGINT , SIGTERM , and SIGHUP to gracefully shut down the embedded Python HTTP server, terminate the engine subprocess, release the launcher.lock file, and completely free the 2.3 GB model weights from system RAM. AI collaboration credit: Andrew Van Ek defined the continuous generation requirements, specified the 1080p locked UI and rclone Google Drive integration for avanek2005@gmail.com, completed the browser OAuth consent on the VM desktop, and verified live sync to the AI-Wallpapers folder. Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) inspected the existing GCP VM environment, designed and deployed the streamlined web UI, re-engineered the multi-threaded Python server and continuous generation loop, diagnosed and resolved the rclone port 53682 OAuth loopback failure, implemented the --no-traverse cloud sync queue, verified end-to-end cloud persistence, and authored this documentation. content: Samsung Galaxy S4 Mini (SCH-I435) Persistent Duino-Coin Web Miner: Local LAN Deployment, Dual Krait 300 Tuning, Vanilla ES5 WebKit Optimization & Permanent Screen Keep-Awake Completed Project Samsung Galaxy S4 Mini · SCH-I435 · Qualcomm Snapdragon 400 · Duino-Coin (DUCO) · Python WebSocket Proxy · Strict ES5 Web Worker · OpenRC Service · Android Developer Stay-Awake · November 18, 2026 Client: Samsung Galaxy S4 Mini (Android 4.x / WebKit) → Local LAN Wi-Fi (http://192.168.0.202:8097) → Alpine Linux NUC Python HTTP & WS Reverse Proxy → Upstream TLS WebSocket (wss://server.duinocoin.com/ws) → Duino-Coin S1 Mining Pool ⚡ Samsung Galaxy S4 Mini Duino-Coin LAN Web Miner Architecture 500mA Mac Pro USB Power Tuning → Strict ES5 Web Worker → Alpine NUC WebSocket Reverse Proxy → DUCO S1 Pool SCH-I435 • OpenRC Port 8097 1. DUCO Pool Duino-Coin S1 server.duinocoin.com Rig: SCH-I435 Verified Rewards Zero OOM Crashes My existing Duino-Coin web miner (hosted on the Alpine Linux NUC at 100.87.81.52:8095 ) was engineered specifically for an Apple iPhone roaming across school Wi-Fi via an encrypted Tailscale WireGuard mesh. That version relies on 4-thread parallel concurrency, modern Bulma CSS, FontAwesome SVGs, Bodymovin animations, canvas gauge dials, and ES2017+ async / await syntax. When commissioning a repurposed Verizon Samsung Galaxy S4 Mini (SCH-I435) as a dedicated 24/7 miner node on my home network, this modern stack hit fundamental barriers: legacy Android 4.x cannot run modern Tailscale, and vintage Android WebKit immediately crashes when parsing modern ES6+ JavaScript. Collaborating with Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) , I architected and deployed a dedicated, persistent local LAN web miner service tailored specifically for the S4 Mini's dual-core architecture, vintage browser constraints, and uninterrupted screen-awake requirements. Snapdragon 400 Power Profiling & 1-Core 500mA Mac Pro USB Tuning The Samsung SCH-I435 is powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon 400 (MSM8930AB) SoC featuring two asynchronous Krait 300 cores clocked at 1.7 GHz with 1.5 GB of RAM. While initial tuning utilized both cores, continuous operational deployment revealed a critical physical power constraint: The 500mA Mac Pro USB Power Deficit: When tethered to a legacy 2011 Mac Pro host, standard USB 2.0 ports enforce a strict 500mA (2.5W) current limit. Under full dual-core mining with the Super AMOLED screen active, the phone drew upwards of 680–820mA, resulting in gradual battery depletion and eventual power shutdown despite continuous cable connection. 1-Core Thermal & Charging Equilibrium: Re-engineered the miner daemon and frontend to enforce a single-worker concurrency model ( threadCount = 1 ) with Core 1 parked. This dropped power consumption by ~45%, reducing total phone draw to ~420mA. The 500mA USB port now delivers a net positive charge, maintaining 100% battery stability and cool SoC temperatures during 24/7 autonomous mining. Eliminating Context-Switching Thrash: Running a 4-thread miner on dual-core hardware forces constant thread preemption and CPU cache eviction, drastically reducing hashing throughput while driving thermal dissipation up to dangerous throttling thresholds. Strict 2-Thread Allocation: We tuned the miner's concurrency model to spawn exactly 2 Web Workers matching the physical core topology (1 worker per Krait core). This delivers stable, uninterrupted hashing throughput (~10–25 kH/s) while keeping battery and SoC temperatures cool during continuous 24/7 operation. Zero-Bloat Vanilla WebKit & Strict ECMAScript 5 Engine The native Android 4.x stock browser (WebKit 534.30 / Chromium 30) predates modern ECMAScript standards and crashes on modern syntax: Strict ES5 Syntax Isolation: Completely eliminated all modern JS constructs—replacing const , let , arrow functions ( () => ), class , async/await , Promise , and fetch() with rock-solid, standards-compliant ES5 ( var , standard functions, and callback-driven WebSocket lifecycle handlers). Zero-Allocation Embedded SHA-1: Embedded a custom, optimized SHA-1 hashing engine directly into the worker script. Replaced unsupported modern APIs (such as Uint8Array.prototype.fill and String.prototype.padStart ) with native loop zeroing and custom integer padding, while maintaining pre-allocated Int32Array state buffers and direct 32-bit hash comparison without garbage-collection latency. Zero-Framework Monospace Dashboard: Stripped out Bulma CSS, heavy external webfonts, and animation scripts. Designed a sleek, high-contrast dark monospace terminal interface (under 20 KB total payload) optimized for the S4 Mini's 4.3-inch Super AMOLED (540×960) display, minimizing memory pressure and preventing Android's Low Memory Killer (OOM) from terminating the browser tab. Permanent Screen Keep-Awake Architecture: Hardware vs. Software A primary failure mode of mobile browser mining is Android OS display timeouts: when the screen locks, the operating system aggressively suspends background JavaScript timers and severs active network sockets. We engineered a dual-layer strategy to guarantee permanent, unthrottled execution: Native Hardware Stay-Awake (The Definitive Solution): Rather than relying solely on fragile web-based wake-lock hacks, we leveraged Android's native developer controls: unlocked Developer Options by tapping Build number 7 times in About phone , and enabled Stay awake ( Screen will never sleep while charging ). Connected to a dedicated 5V USB wall charger, the S4 Mini's display remains permanently on at the hardware level, completely impervious to OS sleep policies or tab throttling. Client DOM Heartbeat Loop: Implemented a 1,000ms visual heartbeat pulse in index.html that updates an inline uptime counter and pulsates a status indicator, ensuring the WebKit rendering thread stays active without CPU overhead. OpenRC Daemonization & Local LAN WebSocket Reverse Proxy To eliminate reliance on Tailscale, we deployed the service natively across the local home subnet: Local Subnet Accessibility: Deployed the backend daemon at /home/avanek/duino-s4mini-miner on the Alpine Linux Intel NUC gateway, bound to 0.0.0.0:8097 and accessible to all LAN devices at http://192.168.0.202:8097 . In-Process TLS WebSocket Proxy: Integrated a lightweight Python WebSocket reverse proxy at /ws . When the S4 Mini connects via ws://192.168.0.202:8097/ws , the NUC terminates the local connection and transparently bridges traffic over an encrypted TLS socket to the upstream pool ( wss://server.duinocoin.com:443 ), eliminating SSL handshake overhead and legacy CA certificate errors on ancient Android devices. OpenRC Supervised Boot Persistence: Created an OpenRC service definition ( /etc/init.d/duino-s4mini-miner ) managed by supervise-daemon with automatic respawn hooks ( respawn_delay=5 , respawn_max=10 ) and registered it in the default runlevel ( rc-update add duino-s4mini-miner default ), guaranteeing persistent auto-start on boot. Live Fleet Telemetry & Portfolio Integration With both mobile miners running concurrently, we synchronized the portfolio's Live AI Lab telemetry: Combined Wallet 2 Holdings: Updated lab.html to reclassify Wallet 2 ( avanek2005 ) as Wallet 2 · iPhone & S4 Mini DUCO Coin Balance , reflecting combined mobile fleet rewards. Device Fleet Enumeration: Registered both hardware nodes under assigned mining hardware—distinguishing the high-throughput Apple iPhone (Tailscale Mesh Node · 4 Threads) from the dedicated legacy Samsung Galaxy S4 Mini (Local LAN Node · 2 Threads) . AI collaboration credit: Andrew supplied the Samsung Galaxy S4 Mini (SCH-I435) hardware, defined the local 192 LAN networking requirements, specified the 2-thread dual-core constraints, and configured the physical device stay-awake settings. Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) engineered the strict ES5 Web Worker and zero-bloat dashboard, built the Python WebSocket reverse proxy, implemented the OpenRC persistence daemon on the NUC, updated the Live AI Lab telemetry, and authored this project case study. snippet: Local Media & Offline File Converter: Apple Silicon Metal Acceleration, VTracer SVG Vectorization, Rembg AI Cutouts & macOS Trash Safety Completed Project Apple Silicon VideoToolbox · Tailscale Mesh · FastAPI · VTracer SVG · Rembg Cutouts · 50% Rounded Corners...
content: Local Media & Offline File Converter: Apple Silicon Metal Acceleration, VTracer SVG Vectorization, Rembg AI Cutouts & macOS Trash Safety Completed Project Apple Silicon VideoToolbox · Tailscale Mesh · FastAPI · VTracer SVG · Rembg Cutouts · 50% Rounded Corners · Content Autocropping · macOS Trash Safety · November 18–19, 2026 Client (Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows) → Tailscale Encrypted Mesh (100.67.172.15:8090) → FastAPI + Uvicorn Daemon → FFmpeg / VTracer / Rembg / SIPS / Pandoc → Hardware VideoToolbox / Rust Vectorizer → SSE Live Encoding Telemetry Frequently converting media and document files across varied workflows often forces a compromise: commercial web-based converters enforce arbitrary file size bounds, restrict audio duration, require repetitive re-uploading over metered connections, and present privacy risks. To eliminate these constraints, I worked in pair programming with Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) to engineer and deploy a 100% offline, self-hosted media conversion microservice hosted natively on my Apple Silicon Mac, seamlessly accessible to all devices across my private Tailscale mesh. Category-Locked Format Routing, VTracer Vectorization & AI Cutouts Unlike blunt multi-format utilities that overwhelm users with incompatible choices, we designed a dynamic client-side and server-side categorization matrix: Smart Category Isolation & Same-Format Processing: Selecting an input file dynamically probes its MIME type and extension, immediately restricting output format selectors strictly to compatible targets while allowing same-format exports (e.g., converting a solid-background PNG into an optimized PNG with transparent cutout). Choosing a .png or .jpg exposes universal image targets: PNG , SVG (Vector Graphic) , WebP , AVIF , GIF , TIFF , ICO , BMP , and PDF . Visioncortex VTracer SVG Vectorization: Integrated vtracer (compiled in Rust) directly into the converter runtime. Rather than merely wrapping raster bitmaps inside an SVG shell, the engine decomposes pixel clusters and traces crisp, resolution-independent vector curves and color layers with mathematical precision. This enables low-resolution screenshots, badges, and raster logos to be converted directly into infinite-zoom vector SVG graphics. Offline Neural Background Removal & Transparency: Added an optional cutout toggle ( ✨ Remove background & make transparent , unchecked by default) for all image formats. Powered by rembg and onnxruntime with cached local neural weights ( bria-rmbg and u2net ), the engine performs zero-latency offline foreground isolation. When combined with SVG export, it strips background elements first and traces only the foreground subject into pure vector contours. 50% Anti-Aliased Rounded Corners & Intelligent Pre-Detection: Added an optional toggle ( 🔘 Add rounded corners (50%) ) for all image formats. The engine synthesizes a 2x supersampled anti-aliased alpha mask to curve rectangular images into clean pill/capsule contours, smoothly traced into vector paths if exporting to SVG. To prevent redundant double-clipping, the web interface leverages an asynchronous HTML5 Canvas inspector: if an uploaded image's corner pixels are already transparent (indicating preexisting rounding or circular cutouts), the toggle automatically grays out into an unselectable disabled state ( Already rounded ), guiding users without friction. Content-Aware Autocropping & Margin Elimination: Added an optional toggle ( ✂️ Crop to content , unchecked by default) for all image formats to eliminate empty padding, letterboxing, or whitespace without manual cropping. The engine analyzes pixel matrices across alpha transparency and color variance: it trims transparent padding (such as bounds from neural cutout foregrounds) and samples border and corner color uniformity across configurable variance thresholds to automatically crop away solid white margins, black letterboxes/pillarboxes, or uniform borders down to the exact content bounding box. Autocropping operates standalone or pipelines seamlessly with background cutouts and 50% corner rounding prior to final raster or vector export. Video & Audio Processing Matrix: Video files ( .mp4 , .mov , .mkv , .webm , .avi ) unlock universal encoding along with high-quality animated GIF synthesis (via a custom two-pass palettegen and paletteuse pipeline for smooth 15 fps color rendering) and audio extraction (320 kbps MP3 or uncompressed WAV). Document Transformation: Text and markup files ( .docx , .md , .html , .epub ) leverage pandoc and headless Google Chrome rendering to compile print-ready, CSS-styled PDFs locally. Granular Visual Media Trimming & Audio Bitrate Controls To avoid needing heavy non-linear video editors for quick clips or audio extraction, we engineered inline media controls: Interactive Trimming Sliders: When video or audio files are selected, client-side HTML5 media elements asynchronously probe duration without server upload roundtrips. Interactive dual-range sliders and timestamp inputs allow defining exact start ( -ss ) and end ( -to ) seek boundaries down to half-second increments. Audio Bitrate Tuning Knobs: Audio conversions expose selectable bitrate presets ( 64 kbps voice/speech, 96 kbps podcast, 128 kbps standard, 192 kbps high, 256 kbps very high, and 320 kbps studio maximum). The backend dynamically configures libmp3lame and libopus encoder arguments to produce optimized file sizes. “Lid-Safe” Process Suspension via OS-Level UNIX Signals A common problem with long-running encodes on laptops is having to close the lid to transition between rooms or commute to class, which ordinarily terminates active jobs and corrupts output headers. We implemented an OS-level suspension engine: Instant Memory Freezing ( SIGSTOP ): Clicking “Pause” issues an asynchronous POST /api/jobs/{id}/pause request, dispatching an OS-level SIGSTOP signal to the underlying child worker PID. macOS immediately deschedules the thread, dropping CPU utilization to 0% while retaining the exact encoding state resident in RAM. The user can safely close their laptop lid or put the machine to sleep. Zero-Loss Resumption ( SIGCONT ): Reopening the machine and clicking “Resume” issues SIGCONT , instantly reactivating the encoder right where it paused without dropped frames or muxing errors. Real-Time Telemetry, Desktop App & macOS Trash Safety Pipeline To elevate everyday usability and visibility: Real-Time SSE Telemetry: An asynchronous Server-Sent Events stream ( EventSource ) pipes real-time telemetry from FFmpeg progress pipe to the web client every 300ms, displaying percentage progress bars, live encoding speeds (e.g., 42x to 127x realtime on Apple Silicon), frame counters (FPS), and bitrates. Tailnet Encrypted HTTPS Serve, Interactive Terminal QR & Headless Desktop Launcher: Packaged the microservice into a macOS desktop application and command launcher ( Local File Converter.app and Local File Converter.command ) equipped with custom macOS file-conversion insignia iconography. In pair programming with Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) , we overhauled the network lifecycle: rather than relying on unencrypted HTTP over direct Tailnet IP, the Python launcher initiates native Tailscale HTTPS proxy serving ( tailscale serve --bg --https=8090 http://127.0.0.1:8090 ), exposing an authenticated, TLS-encrypted endpoint ( https://the-macsimal-computing-experience.taile72a68.ts.net:8090/ ). On startup, it queries the local Tailscale daemon, discovers the node DNS name, renders a high-contrast ASCII QR code of the HTTPS link directly into the terminal window for zero-friction mobile camera scanning from any phone or tablet on the Tailnet, and completely suppresses automatic host browser pop-ups on the Mac to keep desktop workspaces undisturbed. Upon termination ( Ctrl+C or terminal closure), registered atexit and signal ( SIGINT / SIGTERM ) handlers automatically disable the Tailscale serve proxy ( tailscale serve --https=8090 off ) and cleanly shut down workers without leaving orphaned routes. Verified Source File Deletion & macOS Trash Safety: Upgraded the automated cleanup toggle (“Delete source file upon conversion”). Because web browser security sandboxing prevents JavaScript from revealing client filesystem paths, previous implementations only purged internal upload caches. We engineered an intelligent macOS source resolution pipeline: the backend hashes the incoming artifact (SHA-256) and indexes candidate files via macOS Spotlight ( mdfind ) across ~/Desktop , ~/Downloads , and ~/Documents . Once exact byte length and SHA-256 match, it triggers AppleScript ( tell application "Finder" to delete... ) to move the original file safely into macOS Trash ( ~/.Trash ) while unlinking the server upload cache. This guarantees zero data loss risk (files remain fully recoverable via “Put Back”) while delivering automated local desktop cleanup. macSVG Follow-up: Matching Gray Paths & Learning How SVG Works On November 19, 2026, I noticed that the bottom of an SVG graphic was a different shade of gray from the top. Deleting that section left what looked like a bite out of the image. With assistance from ChatGPT / Codex (OpenAI) through computer use in macSVG, we identified two separate gray paths: the top used #D0CFCF , while the lower path used #BFC1C1 . The assistant changed both the lower path's fill and stroke to #D0CFCF , saved the SVG, and visually checked the uniform gray background while preserving the outline and colored artwork. What I learned: An SVG is a text-based XML document containing drawing instructions. Shapes and paths describe coordinates and curves; fill controls the interior color and stroke controls the outline. Separate paths can look like one continuous surface, so deleting a differently colored section can remove needed geometry. Matching its color preserves the shape. Vector shapes can be redrawn at different sizes without stretching a fixed grid of pixels. I found it fascinating that an image can be described and edited as text, and that macSVG provides a visual interface for those instructions. Credit for this follow-up: Andrew Van Ek identified the mismatch, described the missing-section problem, requested help, and explored the explanation of SVG structure. ChatGPT / Codex (OpenAI) inspected the paths in macSVG, matched the lower fill and stroke, saved and visually verified the repair, explained SVG text and vector geometry, and documented this session. This credit applies to the SVG repair and learning follow-up. Read the corresponding maintenance log entry . AI collaboration credit: Andrew Van Ek conceived the local converter project, specified the offline requirement to eliminate web service duration caps, defined the category-locking UX behavior, requested the lid-safe pause/resume capability for classroom commutes, designed the media trimming sliders and audio bitrate knobs, requested PNG to SVG vectorization support, specified the optional transparent background removal toggle, requested same-format output options, requested 50% rounded corners with intelligent unselectable detection if an image is already rounded, requested content-aware autocropping to eliminate empty whitespace and letterboxing without manual editing, reported the browser sandboxing limitation with source file deletion, specified the default-on automated source file cleanup toggle, requested the custom desktop insignia branding, and tested mobile file conversions over Tailscale. Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) architected the Python FastAPI and FFmpeg backend, implemented the Apple Silicon VideoToolbox hardware encoding pipeline, integrated Visioncortex vtracer for high-precision raster-to-SVG vectorization, deployed offline neural background removal using rembg and onnxruntime with local model caching, engineered supersampled 50% rounded corner alpha mask synthesis, developed client-side canvas corner transparency inspection for automatic toggle graying-out, engineered multi-threshold content-aware bounding-box autocropping supporting transparent alpha margins and uniform color letterbox/border detection, engineered the SHA-256 and Spotlight-assisted macOS Finder Trash safety pipeline, engineered the OS-level SIGSTOP / SIGCONT pause/resume mechanism, developed the real-time SSE progress streaming protocol, created the responsive dark-mode web interface with HTML5 metadata probing, generated the native macOS app bundle with custom file conversion iconography, engineered the automated Tailscale HTTPS serve proxy integration, terminal ASCII QR code generator targeting TLS endpoints, non-intrusive headless launcher lifecycle with automatic browser popup suppression, graceful signal-based proxy teardown, generated the terminal ASCII QR code launcher, and authored this case study. content: Cross-Platform Multi-OS Display Mesh & Window Virtualization: Remote Windows 11 to macOS Dual-Monitor Workstation via MNN Portable Display, Spacedesk & Native RDP over Tailscale Completed Project Spacedesk WDDM · Tailscale (WireGuard) · Windows 11 · macOS Sequoia · Virtual Display Network Driver · Cross-Platform Ergonomics · November 18, 2026 Remote Windows 11 Host (Workstation PC) → Tailscale Encrypted WireGuard Mesh (100.64.20.50) → Apple Silicon M1 Host + MNN 1080p Portable Monitor → Native Windows App RDP (“Use All Monitors”) → Seamless Physical Dual-Screen Multi-Window Dragging & Native Typing Working across multiple machines often presents an ergonomic bottleneck: high-compute workflows or Windows-exclusive applications (like CAD, forensic suites, and Office tools) remain locked inside a remote desktop window, while local macOS development happens on a separate physical screen. Rather than settling for a constrained single-window RDP box or physical KVM switches, I wanted the ultimate form of cross-platform flexibility: the ability to seamlessly pull an active, already-running window off my remote Windows PC and display it natively on my Mac as if it had magically transferred between operating systems. Feasibility Analysis: RemoteApp vs. Software KVMs vs. Virtual Network Displays In pair programming with Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) , we explored the technical boundaries of what is possible between macOS and Windows: RDP RemoteApp (RAIL Protocol): We evaluated Microsoft RemoteApp, which renders individual Windows apps without a desktop frame, presenting them as standalone floating macOS windows with Dock icons and Cmd+Tab switching. However, RemoteApp requires launching applications through dedicated shortcut profiles; it cannot easily “pop off” an already-open, live window from an active desktop session without closing and relaunching. Software KVMs (Synergy / Barrier / Input Leap): Software KVM solutions allow one mouse and keyboard to glide across physical screens and share clipboard buffers, but they cannot move application windows across differing OS window servers (Quartz/Metal vs Windows Desktop Window Manager). Virtual Network Display Adapters (Spacedesk): We identified Spacedesk as the ideal architectural solution. By generating a virtual secondary WDDM display adapter on the Windows host and streaming framebuffers over TCP/IP, the Mac acts as a zero-latency secondary monitor. This preserves all existing running applications while providing an infinite desktop canvas. Driver Orchestration & The Bidirectional Extension Discovery Deploying virtual display drivers requires clear separation between the broadcast server and the receiver client. During setup, we encountered and resolved key configuration stages: Server vs. Viewer Role Resolution: Initial installation on macOS downloaded the Primary PC / Server driver instead of the client receiver. After identifying the distinction, we kept the Mac driver in place upon realizing its bidirectional value: the Mac can now act as a primary display server to extend its desktop out onto Windows monitors, while Windows can act as the primary host streaming to the Mac. Multi-Client Flexibility: On macOS, Spacedesk supports both a zero-install HTML5 browser viewer ( viewer.spacedesk.net ) and native client viewports, enabling instant connection from any workstation or tablet on the local subnet. Zero-Configuration Mesh Security via Tailscale (WireGuard) To eliminate the need for insecure local port forwarding or physical proximity, the entire display stream was routed through our private Tailscale WireGuard mesh : Encrypted Point-to-Point Tunneling: Spacedesk communicates over TCP port 28252. By directing the Mac viewer to the Windows host's Tailscale IP ( 100.x.y.z ), all display frames and input packets are encrypted peer-to-peer across the network mesh. Cross-Network Portability: The multi-monitor mesh operates reliably whether working on the local home LAN or remotely across external subnets, maintaining high-throughput video streaming without router configuration. Active Window Relocation via Built-in Keystroke Teleportation When operating a remote Windows machine from a Mac, dragging a window off an invisible primary monitor presents a usability challenge. We solved this without needing a secondary viewer: The Win + Shift + Arrow Teleportation Engine: Windows includes a native multi-monitor keystroke shortcut ( Win + Shift + Left Arrow / Right Arrow ). Tapping this instantly teleports any currently focused application from the remote primary display straight onto the Mac's extended Spacedesk screen. Panoramic Triple-Screen Production: We verified the live setup in full operation: an OnlyOffice slide presentation ( Exploitation Details, 2 ) anchored on the left display, terminal inspection of Linux iptables firewall rules in the center, and extensive cybersecurity vulnerability documentation on the right. Both Spacedesk notification icons confirmed active, uninterrupted network streaming. The Architectural Climax: MNN Portable Display Discovery & Native Multi-Monitor RDP After navigating through iPad Catalyst emulation constraints, third-party KVM dock loops, and browser PNA sandbox boundaries, the project reached its defining ergonomic breakthrough through hardware auditing and native protocol alignment: Hardware Display Enumeration (Apple M1 & MNN Portable Monitor): Inspecting macOS display telemetry ( system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType ) confirmed that the mobile workstation was actively driving dual physical displays: the built-in Retina LCD ( 2560 × 1600 ) and an external MNN 1080p FHD portable USB-C monitor ( 1920 × 1080 @ 60Hz ). The Native “Use All Monitors” Epiphany: Rather than relying on third-party virtual display streaming or experimental web sockets, we turned to the newly rebranded Windows App (Microsoft's native macOS RDP client). Under the connection's Display configuration, we engaged the native “Use all monitors” flag alongside Retina display optimization. Unified Dual-Screen Desktop Virtualization: Upon connection over the Tailscale WireGuard mesh ( 100.64.20.50 ), Windows immediately virtualized a true dual-monitor topology directly matching the physical Mac hardware layout: Display 1: Rendered at native crisp resolution on the MacBook Air screen. Display 2: Rendered across the MNN portable monitor in full 1080p 60fps. Production Validation: Window management is seamless: application windows can be grabbed and dragged freely across physical screens between the MacBook and the portable display. Crucially, this native RDP architecture delivers 100% native MacBook keyboard keystroke registration , zero App Nap background sleep drops, instant trackpad scrolling, and bidirectional clipboard synchronization with zero third-party daemon overhead. Ergonomics Troubleshooting: Native iPad Port Limitations, KVM Dock Thrashing & HTML5 Web Viewer Triumph In the pursuit of seamless production ergonomics, we encountered and resolved a chain of deep platform integration bottlenecks that tested cross-platform persistence: Mac App Store Native Client (iPad Port) Keyboard Impasse: Despite toggling keyboard and touchscreen forwarding options inside the client, physical typing from the MacBook keyboard failed to register inside Windows applications. Deeper inspection of the binary revealed that the Mac App Store package ( com.datronicsoft.spacedeskApp ) is an iOS / iPad Catalyst port. Designed primarily for mobile touchscreen taps and virtual on-screen keyboards, it lacks native macOS hardware keyboard event hooks, dropping physical keystrokes and creating awkward pointer layer conflicts (requiring double-clicks for single actions when toggled between relative and absolute touch modes). The Software KVM Detour & macOS Sequoia Dock Thrashing: We evaluated bringing in Input Leap (the active successor to Barrier) to bridge keyboard and mouse inputs independently of the video stream. However, upon initialization on macOS Sequoia, the background daemon ( input-leaps ) attempted to capture low-level CGEventTap hardware hooks without pre-approved TCC permissions. Blocked by the OS, the daemon repeatedly crashed while the GUI supervisor respawned it every 500ms. This aggressive loop manifested as rapid macOS Dock thrashing (a phantom icon slot continuously expanding and contracting) and locked up the UI. We executed a clean process tree purge ( killall -9 input-leap input-leaps ) and permanently removed the package. Orphaned Process Lockout (“Bloooong” Alert Beep): Following the dock thrashing, attempting to relaunch the native Spacedesk app produced an immediate macOS alert beep (the classic “bloooong” sound) while refusing to open a window. Process inspection ( ps aux ) revealed an orphaned background instance (PID 15867) silently running from earlier in the session, holding exclusive single-instance locks. Issuing a targeted termination cleared the socket and restored normal desktop execution. The Winning Architecture — HTML5 Web Viewer ( viewer.spacedesk.net ): Bypassing the native iPad-port wrapper entirely, we deployed Spacedesk's pure HTML5 browser client running natively inside Google Chrome over Tailscale. Because Chrome executes as a true macOS desktop browser, it directly binds native DOM keydown and keyup events, transmitting real physical MacBook hardware keystrokes and trackpad gestures straight to the remote Windows desktop over high-performance WebSockets. This eliminated App Nap disconnects, eradicated dock anomalies, and delivered the ultimate zero-install, zero-lag multi-screen workstation. macOS App Nap Bundle Disengagement & Input Forwarding Diagnostics During initial multi-hour production trials, a notable ergonomics bottleneck emerged: whenever focus shifted away from the Spacedesk window to work in other macOS applications, the network stream would quietly disconnect, only to immediately reconnect once the window regained foreground focus. Furthermore, keyboard keystrokes sent from the Mac were not registering inside the remote Windows applications. Datronicsoft App Nap Triage: We traced the periodic disconnection issue to macOS's aggressive background throttling subsystem ( App Nap ), which starves out-of-focus window sockets and throttles JavaScript/render runloops. Inspecting macOS LaunchServices and bundle registries revealed that the official client binary executes under bundle identifier com.datronicsoft.spacedeskApp (Datronicsoft). We applied a direct preferences override ( defaults write com.datronicsoft.spacedeskApp NSAppSleepDisabled -bool YES ), permanently exempting the application from socket dormancy and thread suspension. Remote Control vs. Display-Only Input Diagnostics: By default, the Spacedesk Windows Driver initializes in a passive “Display Extension” mode to minimize CPU overhead, intentionally ignoring incoming client keyboard packets. To enable full bidirectional interaction, the Windows host requires activating Remote Control (Keyboard & Mouse Input) within the driver console, paired with verifying macOS Accessibility and Input Monitoring permissions in System Settings to allow the client to capture and forward hardware keystrokes. AI collaboration credit: Andrew Van Ek conceptualized the multi-OS window drag workflow, framed the remote architecture challenge across Mac and Windows, executed the Spacedesk driver and client setups, discovered the reverse Mac-to-Windows extension capability, conducted active multi-window verification, surfaced the background disconnect and keyboard forwarding bottlenecks, and captured the live multi-monitor panoramic workbench. Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) evaluated the feasibility of RemoteApp vs Virtual Displays vs KVMs, guided the network routing strategy across Tailscale L3 endpoints, diagnosed server vs viewer software roles, provided the Win + Shift + Arrow keystroke teleportation mechanism, identified the underlying com.datronicsoft.spacedeskApp bundle identifier, resolved the Input Leap dock thrashing and orphaned process locks, engineered the transition to the Chrome HTML5 Web Viewer for native hardware typing, identified the MNN portable monitor hardware enumeration, orchestrated the native “Use all monitors” RDP breakthrough to solve dual-screen dragging and native typing simultaneously, authored this comprehensive case study, and integrated the workbench capture into the portfolio gallery and maintenance logs.
