By downloading and analyzing dual-channel carrier recordings ( RE90eba4c1a36d59e00191a861a11291af ) and executing real-time simulated audio streaming through VoiceSession , Antigravity AI isolated why the AI connected but remained silent across the 22-second call: the 6.5-second outbound greeting delay was canceled immediately by the initial automated IVR prompt, subsequent loud hold music (peaking over 9,000 RMS) falsely triggered in-flight speech interruption and aborted local model generation, and when a live representative (“Chloe”) answered, the 1,600 ms turn-silence detection and model turnaround left dead air, causing her to hang up before Arthur's cue and speech could play. To ensure prompt engagement and prevent hang-ups, we re-engineered conversational timing: shortened the outbound greeting delay from 6.5s to 1.8s, tightened the endpoint detector's silence threshold from 1,600 ms down to 850 ms, and accelerated the thinking cue ( “Hmm.” ) delay from 1,000 ms to 400 ms so audible conversational feedback begins in under half a second. Additionally, we expanded the voice pool from 5 to 12 distinct older-victim personas leveraging installed macOS system voices across US and UK accents (Arthur, Walter, Dorothy, Edith, George, Margaret, Harold, Florence, Edward, Evelyn, Helen, and Frank) with automatic non-repeating randomization between consecutive calls. All 49 automated unit and regression tests passed cleanly. Live adversarial hold-queue survival, zero-latency hearing fast-path & extended filler phrasing with Antigravity AI: A subsequent live adversarial call to the solar scam line verified the timing improvements in action. The persona system randomly assigned George (Grandpa (English (UK))), connected through the IVR, endured a 33-second hold queue, and triggered the thinking cue in exactly 402 ms when a live representative picked up asking “Hello? Can you hear me properly? Hello?” George successfully formulated and delivered his response ( “Hello. I’m George. Could you explain what the message is about?” ). However, turn-by-turn timestamps revealed that the 0.74s “Hmm.” left a 3.5s silent gap while the Apple Foundation Model completed inference (4.2s total), causing the representative to disconnect just as George began speaking. Working with Antigravity AI, we resolved this latency bottleneck on two fronts: first, we engineered a deterministic zero-latency fast-path in reply() for connection and audibility checks ( “Can you hear me?” , “Are you there?” , “Hello? Hello?” ), immediately confirming audibility and restating the case opening with 0 ms model delay; second, we upgraded the thinking cue to an extended, realistic conversational filler ( “Hmm... let me see here.” , spanning 2.04 seconds) followed by an intentional 250 ms natural breath pause before delivering generated dialogue. This completely bridges the on-device inference window with lifelike senior hesitation, ensuring scammers stay engaged on the line. Multi-line caller ID pool and automated anti-blacklist number rotation: To prevent scammers and boiler-room call centers from burning or blacklisting our primary outbound line during sustained testing, I expanded the telephony configuration into a multi-line Caller ID pool with Antigravity AI. We provisioned a secondary Twilio line (+1 316 241-1022, Kansas) alongside our original number (+1 848 356-5053, New Jersey) and updated server.mjs to support an environment variable pool ( TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBERS ). Outbound calls now dynamically cycle through the pool via non-repeating random selection ( pickOutboundNumber ), guaranteeing that consecutive attempts rotate across different regional area codes. This provides tactical resilience against call-center blocklists while maintaining centralized call logs, carrier dual-channel recording, and signed webhook routing. Cyber-defense favicon suite and web branding with Antigravity AI: To polish the dashboard experience and provide clean tab and home-screen recognition, I designed and generated a custom brand favicon suite with Antigravity AI. Centered on the platform’s tactical slate-and-lime aesthetic, the vector icon combines a defense shield with an angled telephone handset and dual-ring radar intercept waves in electric lime ( #c9f26d ) against a dark squircle ( #101214 ). We deployed scalable vector assets ( favicon.svg ), raster icons ( favicon.png , favicon.ico ), and high-resolution iOS touch icons ( apple-touch-icon.png ), updated server.mjs static route serving and Content Security Policy headers ( img-src 'self' data: ), and linked the icon set in index.html . Hold queue suppression, voice modernization & operator telemetry with Antigravity AI: Follow-up live call adversarial traces against active solar and debt-relief scam lines (+1 231-432-8587 and +1 877-655-0103) revealed that carrier hold and queue transfer announcements ( “Your call is important to us, please hold for our next representative” ) were previously endpointed as caller turns, causing the AI to fire its thinking filler and converse with hold music. With Antigravity AI, I engineered automated hold and queue prompt detection ( isHoldPrompt ) that suppresses LLM inference and thinking cues during transfers, holding the AI in silent anticipation until a live human answers. Additionally, replaced legacy formant-based novelty voices (Grandma and Grandpa) across all 12 personas with modern, high-definition UK and US speech synthesizers (Flo, Eddy, Reed, Shelley, Rocko, Samantha, and Daniel) to eliminate acoustic aliasing and robotic crackle. In the web interface, configured automated desktop expansion for the live transcript panel and enhanced the call workspace header to persistently display the active dialed phone number alongside persona metadata for rapid dead-number triage and case-log removal. Automated bulk case ingestion, E.164 normalization & target pool prefilling with Antigravity AI: To eliminate manual case-entry friction and accelerate operational triage during adversarial dialing campaigns, I collaborated with Antigravity AI to engineer an automated ingestion and normalization pipeline for curated scam intelligence. Parsing unformatted telephone records and field intelligence directly from an operational target dossier ( it's_the_scam_List.docx ), Antigravity AI constructed a multi-pass regex extraction engine that resolved 172 unique phone numbers into standardized international E.164 notation (e.g., +13652925579 ). The ingestion system automatically synthesized concise, high-context operational labels (classifying Grandparent bail-out scams, Publishers Clearing House impersonators, Nigerian check advance schemes, bank fraud alerts, and pet/escort scams across AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, Bell Mobility, Rogers, Telus, and Dish Wireless), preserved crucial IVR bypass instructions (such as dialing * or # to skip greetings and dead-air prompts), embedded historical carrier verification telemetry (e.g., Verified: 11/5 and 11/6 ), and stripped web URLs to enforce strict compliance with backend contextError guardrails. Atomically merged into the persistent dashboard store ( data/state.json ) with automated timestamped backups, the system expanded the operator target pool to 176 prefilled cases ready for instantaneous one-touch dialing, dynamic persona assignment, and rapid dead-number retirement. Persistent session telemetry, live operator dashboard metrics & Tailscale portfolio sync with Antigravity AI: To monitor cumulative operational impact across weeks of adversarial calling, I collaborated with Antigravity AI to build a persistent metrics and cross-node telemetry pipeline. We implemented a durable analytics store in data/state.json that preserves total calls placed (116), adversarial airtime (73 minutes / 4,367 seconds), voicemails delivered (22), and active targets (176) across server restarts and crashes. In the web dashboard, we introduced a responsive 4-pill live status bar in index.html styled with tactical lime borders and subtle glassmorphic backdrops, updated automatically via WebSocket event summaries. To showcase these adversarial counter-operations on my public portfolio, Antigravity AI designed a dedicated “Scam Defense AI Telemetry” card and node status badge on the “Stats for Nerds” page ( stats.html ), and authored an automated background sync utility ( scripts/sync-portfolio-stats.sh ) triggered inside launch-dashboard.command . Every time the dashboard launches on my Mac, it verifies passwordless Tailscale SSH connectivity to the Alpine Linux NUC ( avanek@100.87.81.52 ), synchronizes the latest call totals and active target counts into stats.html , executes automated pre-commit search index regeneration, and pushes updates to GitHub without blocking local operator workflows. Voicemail beep gate synchronization, carrier playout flush & suburban persona hardening with Antigravity AI: Live adversarial field testing against a Publishers Clearing House prize scam line (+1 332-279-7394) highlighted two conversational timing subtleties and an operational detail. The AI persona (Florence) adapted brilliantly to the sweepstakes pitch instead of defaulting to generic debt statements, but turn telemetry revealed that her greeting began speaking over the carrier voicemail beep, and her final words were clipped slightly by an aggressive hangup. Analyzing the audio pipeline, Antigravity AI determined that local Whisper transcription latency (~1.5s) allowed silence frames to accumulate in the VoicemailGate detector while the prompt was processing, falsely satisfying the quiet threshold before the beep sounded. We added an explicit VoicemailGate.reset() trigger at voicemail handover and enforced requireBeep: true in voice-session.mjs to guarantee the AI waits for carrier tone completion. We then widened the onGoodbye REST termination grace period from 300ms to 1500ms in server.mjs , giving Twilio's audio buffer sufficient time to flush complete speech across the PSTN. Finally, to handle scammers who demand a physical mailing address to send fraudulent cashier's checks or prize notices, we assigned unique, believable New Jersey suburban street addresses to all 12 personas in call-profile.mjs (e.g., 612 Meadowbrook Lane in Clark, NJ) and tuned personaPrompt to supply these authentic details naturally under interrogation. Mobile touch keypad, iOS audio playback resilience, instant operator callback speech & voicemail loop resolution with Antigravity AI: Real-world operational field testing on iPhone revealed several critical telephony and mobile ergonomics friction points during live calls. Tapping the desktop DTMF PIN text field triggered iOS Safari’s aggressive viewport auto-zoom (<16px font defect), throwing the entire layout out of alignment; carrier monitoring audio was frequently inaudible due to mobile Safari auto-suspending Web Audio contexts during outbound dialing silence or muting behind the iOS hardware silent switch; the operator manual speech button failed to speak when commanded; and carrier voicemails lacking distinct beep frequencies caused Arthur to wait 30 seconds in dead air until the remote system looped repeated “We didn’t get your message” prompts, triggering speech collision and overspeaking loops. Collaborating with Antigravity AI, we executed a comprehensive architectural overhaul across the frontend, telephony engine, and audio lifecycle. We re-engineered the mobile call actions bar by implementing a giant, high-visibility hangup button ( #stop , 54px min-height, full mobile width), positioned the primary Speak action directly underneath, completely removed the desktop text input field on mobile via CSS media queries, and engineered an intuitive 3×4 responsive touch dialpad ( 1–9 , * , 0 , # ) featuring tactile press animations, instant local DTMF feedback tones, and zero-zoom touch targets for effortless IVR navigation. To conquer iOS audio silencing, we integrated an invisible HTML5 audio session bridge ( AVAudioSessionCategoryPlayback ) and a continuous Web Audio keep-alive buffer loop, guaranteeing call audio streams over the iPhone loudspeaker even if the physical silent switch is engaged or background media was playing, paired with global touch-gesture auto-resume listeners. For the operator speech trigger, we engineered VoiceSession.speakDirect() to deliver a pre-synthesized, zero-latency callback message ( “My name is <name>, call me back at 313-279-8146, and my address is <address>” ) customized to the active persona, immediately clearing line echo and canceling background listeners. Finally, we resolved the voicemail loop by allowing the VoicemailGate to trigger on either a confirmed frequency beep or 3.5 seconds of post-prompt silence, and instituted single-instance execution locks ( voicemailActive / voicemailCompleted ) in server.mjs to permanently prevent duplicate voicemail handlers and speech collisions. All 52 automated tests in the test suite pass with zero regressions. Mobile ergonomics compression, jitter buffer de-crackling, authentic Google Voice disconnect chime & automated mailbox-filling queue with Antigravity AI: Real-world operational testing across 181 live adversarial calls exposed critical ergonomic and audio performance bottlenecks. The operator interface on mobile suffered from vertical overcrowding due to non-essential stats and redundant instructional notices; the test tone was quiet; phone hangup tones lacked realistic carrier acoustics; audio frequently became choppy during continuous speech (such as street address reading); and repeatedly dialing numbers manually to fill scammer voicemail inboxes required constant operator intervention. In pair programming with Antigravity AI, we resolved every defect. We re-engineered the mobile dashboard layout by placing “▪ Hang up call” and “▶ Speak callback info” side-by-side in a responsive 2-column grid with matching 52px heights, moved the Live Transcript directly above the call controls, completely removed the redundant instructional notice banner, and hid the stats panel to recover maximum screen real estate on mobile devices while removing the “Edit context” button on phone screens. In the Web Audio subsystem, we replaced the quiet test tone with a hilarious, loud custom synthesized comic fart sound (utilizing a resonant lowpass filter sweep, sawtooth pitch drop, LFO flutter modulation, and filtered noise burst), integrated the authentic Google Voice descending disconnect chime (B4 493.88Hz → G4 392.00Hz) programmed to trigger automatically whenever a call terminates, and eliminated audio stuttering and crackling during long persona speeches by re-anchoring the jitter buffer without artificial 50ms silence gaps. Furthermore, we engineered automated call stacking: each case in the carousel and log now features an interactive call counter stepper (1–25) and a “Direct Voicemail” mode toggle that bypasses interactive greetings to leave messages instantly. Calls in the queue advance automatically with a 2.5-second pacing delay, and if remote carrier full-mailbox detection triggers ( “Remote mailbox is full” ), the queue aborts immediately with a celebration alert ( “🎯 TARGET MAILBOX FILLED!” ) to conserve minutes. All 52 automated tests in the test suite pass with zero regressions. Public counter-telephony video releases with Antigravity AI: Documenting the 16-call escalation and full mailbox finale against target Andrew Goldberg (+1 737-298-4180), we produced and published two synchronized visual case studies showcasing on-device AI telephony defense: the vertical mobile showcase Filling a Scammer's Voicemail with 16 AI Personas! (YouTube Short) and the full widescreen debrief Operation Mailbox Saturation: 16 AI Personas vs. Jamaican Lottery Scammer (Full Encounter) , featuring live telemetry dashboards, real-time audio visualizers, and carrier saturation confirmation. Desktop split carousel architecture, persistent queueing, barge-in over-speech calibration & dynamic profanity masking with Antigravity AI: Advancing the dashboard beyond mobile ergonomics, live operational calling on Desktop exposed substantial layout friction when managing large adversarial target registries (172 active cases). Scrolling down a massive vertical list was tedious; telephone barge-in threshold (previously 3000 RMS with 800ms initial lockout) occasionally caused persona models to speak over callers on lines like +1 646-671-8077; direct voicemail queues lacked instant live-conversation bailouts when live scammers unexpectedly answered; repeat call counts and voicemail mode toggles reset on page reload; and explicit profanity uttered by hostile scammers appeared unfiltered in live transcripts. Collaborating with Antigravity AI, we resolved every point across the full stack. We abolished the giant vertical desktop list entirely, replacing it with an elegant dual-carousel split architecture: the Target Wagon on the left and the Inactive Recycle Bin Wagon on the right, both featuring snappy card navigation, Prev/Next chevron controls, keyboard arrow bindings, and instant individual restore or permanent deletion. In the active workspace header bar, we integrated a real-time Target Action Pill displaying the active or most recently called number with an instant “✕ Move to Bin” one-click archive button, alongside dedicated “⏹ Cancel Queue” and “⚡ Switch to Live AI (Cancel VM)” controls that allow operators to halt call loops or immediately abort recorded voicemail drops if a human scammer picks up. On Desktop, the dialpad keypad is cleanly hidden while an inline DTMF PIN input is embedded beside the audio controls with Enter-to-send support. In the telephony bridge, we calibrated the voice barge-in detector (reducing RMS energy requirement to 2000, lowering lockout to 450ms, and tightening frame window to 10 frames) to instantly yield when remote speakers talk, widened greeting delay to 2200ms to eliminate answer collisions, and made stepper counts and Direct VM toggles persistently remembered across sessions in browser storage. In the transcript subsystem, we implemented an automated live regex profanity filter that masks offensive language with asterisks, paired with distinct visual styling that color-codes voicemail greeting transcriptions in amber and live conversational speech in tactical lime. All 52 automated tests in the test suite pass with zero regressions. Desktop live controls overhaul, slow-caller turn-taking recalibration, automated callback hangup, voice cadence jitter & Paul Davis counter-telephony video releases with Antigravity AI: Real-world operational testing on active target registries—including live engagements against Publishers Clearing House fake giveaway scammer “Paul Davis” / “Paul Befis” (+1 516-232-6648)—identified subtle interaction hitches and speech collisions. On desktop viewports, the “▪ Hang up call” and “▶ Speak callback info” action buttons occupied an unnecessarily oversized footprint disconnected from the keypad cluster; slow-speaking scammers pausing between sentences were frequently overspoken by the AI due to an overly aggressive 850ms silence timeout; telephony line hiss (<750 RMS) continually reset voicemail silence tracking, requiring manual operator babysitting; clicking the Direct Voicemail mode toggle on carousel cards occasionally failed due to duplicate document-level event listeners; and synthetic voice cadence felt unnaturally uniform across consecutive calls. In pair programming with Antigravity AI, we resolved every defect across the full stack. On desktop viewports, we reorganized the live call controls cluster by moving “▪ Hang up call” and “▶ Speak callback info” directly beneath the inline PIN/digit input field, matching its exact 340px width and scaling button height down to a sleek, compact 38px while preserving full-width, touch-friendly 52px buttons on mobile. In the event system, we removed duplicate click handlers and synchronized the header target action pill to dynamically mirror the actively selected carousel wagon card during idle browsing. In the conversational audio engine, we extended the conversational turn-taking silence threshold from 850ms to 1200ms to comfortably accommodate slow, deliberate speakers, lowered the live barge-in energy threshold from 2000 to 1350 RMS with a 6-frame leaky integrator so caller interruptions immediately halt AI playback, raised the voicemail gate quiet threshold from 500 to 750 RMS to prevent PSTN line noise from resetting silence detection, and wired “▶ Speak callback info” with final: true so the call terminates automatically once playback concludes. To make personas sound authentically human, we engineered runtime voice cadence jitter in createCallProfile , varying speaking rate naturally by ±7 WPM across calls. Furthermore, capturing the 8 live engagements against PCH fake supervisor “Paul Davis” (+1 516-232-6648), we compiled and rendered synchronized dual-channel audio-visual case studies in 16:9 1080p widescreen and 9:16 vertical Shorts, complete with real-time spectrum visualizers, dynamic call counters, the eerie opening voicemail prompt, and sudden scammer hangup moments. All 59 automated unit and integration tests pass with zero regressions. Server-side background calling chains, concurrent duo-telephony voicemail fill, real-time streaming transcripts, and automatic mailbox-full case deletion with Antigravity AI (Revision 0.2.1): As operational field testing scaled into intensive multi-call saturation campaigns, client-side front-end limitations emerged. Placing repeat call chains (5 to 20 calls) previously relied on browser timer execution; navigating away from the dashboard tab or locking a mobile device caused the client runtime to suspend, prematurely stalling pending dial queues. Furthermore, single-line dialing slowed the pace of filling scam voicemail boxes, transcripts dumped text in bulk before speech synthesis had completed, mobile viewports displayed desktop-only controls like the DTMF PIN input group and recycle bin, and target cards whose mailboxes became completely full remained in the active registry. In pair programming with Antigravity AI, we overhauled the system across server and client layers to address every bottleneck. We migrated queue lifecycle management entirely to the server runtime in server.mjs : dial counts, sequence timing, and automatic queue progression are now tracked independently of active browser sessions, ensuring multi-call chains continue unhindered if operators navigate away, switch apps, or refresh their browsers. Leveraging two provisioned Twilio outbound numbers, we engineered concurrent duo-calling for Direct Voicemail mode, automatically advancing repeat counters in blocks of two and dispatching twin simultaneous lines to saturate target mailboxes twice as fast. In the front-end interface, we replaced block transcript insertion with paced, word-by-word streaming matched to audio duration with an active animated typing cursor, accompanied by a dynamic caller speaking pulse wave. To eliminate manual post-campaign cleanup, we introduced an automated mailbox-full purger: when carrier or conversational audio detects remote mailbox exhaustion (“Sorry, the mailbox is full and there is not enough space to leave a message”), the server automatically cancels all remaining queue iterations and permanently purges the target case from the system without sending it to the recycle bin. On mobile viewports, we streamlined the UI by hiding the desktop PIN input and recycle bin drawer, consolidating the call stepper and Direct VM switch onto a single horizontal card row, and removing chevron navigation buttons in favor of native touch swiping. In our live operational test against a Publishers Clearing House fake prize claim line (+1 332-279-7394 spoofing “Todd Sloane, Deborah Holland, Daniella Lam & Howie Guja”), the system executed 50 automated conversational and voicemail saturation calls, successfully exhausting the scammer's storage capacity until the carrier confirmed full mailbox lockout. All 59 automated unit and integration tests pass with zero regressions. Behind the scenes: Architectural breakdown of the 59 automated unit and integration tests: To guarantee that rapid adversarial calling, live carrier handshakes, and local Apple on-device intelligence run with zero crashes or audio clipping, the repository enforces a rigorous 59-test automated validation harness executed across five dedicated suites before any code reaches production. The Audio DSP & Conversational Turn-Taking Suite ( tests/voice.test.mjs , 24 tests) exercises core digital signal processing: it verifies bitwise mathematical conversion between 8kHz telephony G.711 μ-law and 16-bit linear PCM audio without signed amplitude distortion; tests voice activity endpointing using a calibrated leaky integrator to ensure genuine speech triggers turns while line clicks and ambient background noise do not; validates dual-threshold barge-in protection (ignoring hybrid line echo below 3000 RMS while immediately aborting speech when caller energy exceeds 1350 RMS for 6 frames); distinguishes pure single-frequency carrier voicemail beeps (800–1000 Hz) from human vowel formants to prevent premature message drops; tests that dynamic conversational thinking cues (“Hmm...”) play during model latency, stay excluded from history, and instantly cancel if the caller speaks; verifies DTMF menu digit detection (“press 1 for support”); and confirms carrier playback marks acknowledge delivery before advancing conversation state. The Network State Machine Suite ( tests/call-state.test.mjs , 3 tests) protects against real-world cellular packet reordering, guaranteeing that asynchronous Twilio HTTP status callbacks monotonically advance (e.g., preventing late ringing notifications from regressing a connected in-progress stream) and ensuring late REST updates cannot corrupt duplex WebSocket sessions. The Adversarial Persona & Compliance Suite ( tests/profile.test.mjs , 7 tests) validates character integrity: ensuring elder personas (Arthur, Dorothy, Evelyn, Frank) consistently retain their randomized New Jersey street addresses and rates; answering general questions like “Who are you?” with their character identity while strictly enforcing truthful disclosure (“I am an AI voice assistant...”) whenever explicitly asked to preserve transparency; grounding Apple LLM prompts so personas never slip into customer service roles or hallucinate billing claims during prize scam calls; and pacing browser monitor audio at a steady 100ms cadence without packet bursts. The Server Infrastructure & Lifecycle Suite ( tests/server.test.mjs , 2 tests) simulates an entire live telephony session against mocked Twilio carrier endpoints, asserting cryptographic SHA-1 signature authentication, duplex media streaming, operator live audio takeover, and clean Control-C termination without leaving persistent emergency stop flags or orphaned lock files. Finally, the Operational Field Hardening Suite ( tests/enhancements.test.mjs , 23 tests) handles real-world telephone idiosyncrasies: verifying that the VoicemailGate treats carrier line hiss up to 750 RMS as quiet to prevent silence timer resets; asserting that createCallProfile applies natural speech rate jitter (±7 WPM) across calls to eliminate robotic uniformity; validating that Direct Voicemail mode marks outbound audio with final: true to terminate calls immediately upon playback completion; testing live regex profanity masking that asterisks out hostile scammer abuse while preserving transcript legibility; and confirming robust E.164 phone normalization across irregular punctuation, dots, and Unicode formatting. All 59 tests execute deterministically in ~15 seconds with zero flakes or external network dependencies. Client-side JavaScript syntax triage & “Checking AI…” frontend recovery with Antigravity AI: During operational startup testing on November 21, 2026, the dashboard loaded its visual layout but remained permanently frozen with its top status pill stuck displaying “Checking AI…” . Because the terminal startup script displayed [sync-stats] Remote host reachable , initial suspicion centered on remote NUC reachability or local Foundation Model daemon unresponsive states. Collaborating with Antigravity AI, we conducted systematic runtime forensics: we verified that the remote NUC SSH sync script is entirely decoupled from live telephony and that the local Apple Foundation Model health endpoint ( http://127.0.0.1:1976/health ) was healthy and returning HTTP 200. We then ran AST syntax validation against the frontend bundle ( node --check public/app.js ), which immediately pinpointed an uncaught client-side parsing crash ( SyntaxError: Identifier 'text' has already been declared at line 706, alongside an orphaned closing brace at line 882) caused by a duplicate merge within the d.type === 'ended' call completion handler. Because the script failed to parse, the browser halted all JavaScript execution on page load, preventing api('/api/state') from dispatching and stranding the status pill in its initial HTML placeholder state. We refactored the completion handler, eliminated duplicate declarations and redundant playout tone triggers, and verified clean syntax parsing. Following the patch, the client immediately establishes WebSocket duplex telemetry on launch, transitioning the status badge to “AI ready for the next call” , with all server integration tests passing 100%.

content: ACE-Step: Local AI Music Training & Cover Comparisons Completed Milestone (200/200 Epochs) 200 / 200 Epochs Fully Verified (Step 4,600 / 4,600) • Final Checkpoint Loss: 0.8885 (All-Time Low: 0.8650 at Ep 194) • All 200 Intermediate Checkpoints Preserved · Verified October 27, 2026 ACE-Step 1.5 LoRA Training Convergence Telemetry Flow-Matching Velocity Loss vs. 200 Epochs (4,600 Global Steps) • NVIDIA RTX A2000 Laptop GPU Completed: 200 / 200 Epochs Step 4,600 / 4,600 0.80 0.90 1.00 1.10 1.20 1.30 1.40 1.50 Ep 0 s0 Ep 40 s920 Ep 80 s1840 Ep 120 s2760 Ep 160 s3680 Ep 200 s4600 Ep 1: 1.418 (Baseline) Ep 12: 1.002 Ep 31: 0.919 Ep 60: 0.925 Ep 100: 0.889 Ep 140: 0.880 Ep 180: 0.873 Ep 194: 0.865 (All-Time Low) Ep 200: 0.889 (Completed) Cross-Entropy Loss ↓ Training Progress → Milestone Run Global Steps Epoch Range Final Checkpoint Loss Status & Verification Initial Exploratory Step 276 Epochs 1–12 1.0021 ✓ Verified (Preferred hymn cover) Early Continuation Step 345 Epochs 13–15 0.9892 ✓ Verified Extended Overnight 1 Step 1,035 Epochs 16–45 0.9194 (Ep 31) ✓ Verified (NVIDIA RTX A2000 GPU) Deep Overnight 2 Step 1,380 Epochs 46–60 0.8967 (Ep 59) ✓ Verified (First sub-0.90 epoch) Centennial Milestone Step 2,300 Epochs 61–100 0.8893 (Best: 0.8875 ) ✓ Verified (9h 31m runtime) Post-Centennial Push Step 3,220 Epochs 101–140 0.8795 (Ep 140) ✓ Verified (All-time low sub-0.88) Grand Finale 180 Milestone Step 4,140 Epochs 141–180 0.8729 (Ep 154: 0.8700 ) ✓ Verified (180/180 Epochs) Bicentennial 200 Milestone Step 4,600 Epochs 181–200 0.8885 (All-Time Low: 0.8650 at Ep 194) ✓ 100% Completed (200/200 Epochs Verified) I worked with AI to train ACE-Step 1.5 on my Windows computer and explore Christian hard-rock arrangements. I used 89 labeled, roughly 30-second audio clips to train a LoRA, a small add-on that adapts the base music model. My laptop's 4 GB graphics memory meant I had to work carefully to fit the training job without running out of memory. Early runs failed because the model needed more memory than was available, the audio encoder required a separate run on the processor, or the graphics card was busy. I traced the problem to invalid conditioning values, rebuilt that data with BF16 precision and a different attention implementation, and checked all 89 samples for finite values before resuming. Training progressed through twelve epochs, with a separate checkpoint after each pass. Average training loss fell from 1.4179 in epoch one to 1.0021 in epoch twelve. With assistance from Antigravity CLI, I resumed training through epoch fifteen, with loss dropping further to 0.9892 at global step 345, and prepared an authorized 30-epoch extension to reach epoch forty-five (1035 global steps, ~6 hours 15 minutes estimated) to maximize the overnight training window before the Folding@home CPU work unit completes and triggers system shutdown. Following the completion and upload of active Folding@home GPU work units, I launched the authorized 30-epoch continuation run on the dedicated NVIDIA RTX A2000 Laptop GPU to advance from epoch 16 through epoch forty-five (1035 global steps total, ~6 hours 15 minutes estimated). Preflight validation confirmed the restored adapter, optimizer, and scheduler states from the epoch 15 checkpoint, and active training resumed on the GPU with initial step loss reaching 0.9553. Training progressed rapidly, with average epoch checkpoint loss falling to an all-time record of 0.9194 at epoch 31 and 0.9387 at epoch 35, and single-step batch losses regularly dipping below 0.80. To maximize overnight compute, I authorized extending the target from epoch 45 to epoch sixty total (1380 global steps, ~6 additional hours), deploying an automated handover supervisor to smoothly transition the model into epochs 46–60 once epoch 45 completes. Training ran uninterrupted overnight, with single-step batch losses dipping as low as 0.6809 and average epoch checkpoint loss breaking below the 0.90 barrier for the first time at epoch 59 (0.8967). The full 60-epoch run completed successfully at step 1380 with epoch 60 (loss 0.9251), and all 60 intermediate checkpoints were verified with finite weights and preserved for comparative listening evaluation. To maximize the utility of the local GPU before shifting to custom arrangement and vocal experiments, I authorized an additional 40-epoch continuation to reach Epoch 100 total (2,300 global steps). Monitored continuously by an automated supervisor, the pipeline advanced uninterrupted across 9 hours and 31 minutes on the dedicated NVIDIA RTX A2000 Laptop GPU, saving and validating finite adapter weights every 23 steps. Single-step batch loss reached record lows of 0.6288, with checkpoint average loss breaking to an all-time record of 0.8875 at epoch 74 and finishing at 0.8893 at epoch 100. All 100 intermediate checkpoints (84.1 MiB final adapter) have been validated with finite weights and preserved for comparative listening evaluation and upcoming Christian rock vocal style adaptation trials. Following the centennial milestone, I authorized successive continuations on the dedicated NVIDIA RTX A2000 Laptop GPU to achieve deep acoustic convergence. Monitored continuously by an autonomous background supervisor across overnight execution, the pipeline advanced seamlessly through Epochs 101–140 (step 3,220), breaking through previous barriers to attain an average checkpoint loss of 0.8795. The pipeline automatically handed over into Epochs 141–180 (step 4,140), establishing an epoch checkpoint loss of 0.8700 at Epoch 154 before reaching 0.8729 on Epoch 180. To explore the ultimate frontier before overfitting, I authorized the Bicentennial 200 Milestone run advancing through Epochs 181–200 (Step 4,600). The model achieved its all-time lowest epoch checkpoint loss of 0.8650 at Epoch 194 (single-step batch losses reaching 0.6053), concluding cleanly at 0.8885 on Epoch 200. All 200 intermediate checkpoints have been verified with finite weights and preserved on disk for comparative listening and arrangement evaluation. I generated twelve full-length comparison covers, one from each checkpoint, using the same hymn lyrics, reference recording, random seed, duration, and adapter strength. I kept the original comparison separate from later experiments, checked waveform integrity and timing, and used listening notes to compare lyric clarity, phrasing, guitar and drum weight, vocal artifacts, and musical coherence. Epoch twelve was my preferred result in the original set, but still had problems to improve. I then completed three separate generation trials using the epoch-twelve adapter. The first changed the vocal and guitar instructions, adjusted reference influence, and shortened the ending. The result still sounded too soft and did not achieve the intended male vocal character. The second used a different hard-rock song, Lion and the Lamb , as the sole reference. The style improved, but the generated hymn followed that reference's beat and arrangement too closely and stretched words to fit. I rejected the result while preserving its settings, checksums, logs, and listening notes. The third removed source and reference audio entirely and used text-to-music generation with the same epoch-twelve adapter, heavy-rock instructions, and supplied lyrics. Its WAV and MP3 passed finite, non-silent stereo-audio and duration checks. Listening evaluation is still pending to judge vocal quality, natural word timing, arrangement, and the intended style; passing file checks does not establish musical quality. This project has taken patience and persistence through failed runs, memory constraints, long source-encoding stages, full-length generation, and repeated listening reviews. The trials help distinguish the effects of training, reference conditioning, and generation settings. Lower loss alone does not guarantee a better song, and a single trial cannot conclusively explain every artifact.

title: Custom AI: From-Scratch Neural Sequence & Binary Predictor

content: Custom AI: From-Scratch Neural Sequence & Binary Predictor Completed & Live Trained on CPU with PyTorch 2.13 · In-Browser Client-Side Engine · Verified October 24, 2026 From-Scratch CPU Neural Training Convergence Binary Cross-Entropy Loss vs. 120 Epochs • PyTorch 2.13 (CPU) • Cosine Annealing Learning Rate Decay Final Loss: 0.6301 Holdout F1: 55.93% 0.70 0.68 0.66 0.64 0.62 Ep 1: 0.6898 Ep 60: 0.6473 Ep 120: 0.6301 Epoch 1 Epoch 60 Epoch 120 (Final) Binary Cross-Entropy Loss ↓ CPU Optimization Steps → 🧠 Neural Network Architecture & Gradient Flow 14 Input Features → 32 Dense Units (ReLU) → 16 Dense Units (ReLU) → 1 Sigmoid Output • 1,025 Trainable Parameters PyTorch 2.13 (CPU) ← Backpropagation: ∂ℒ/∂W via Chain Rule (Adam Optimizer: α = 0.005 → 0.0005) Input (14-dim) x[t-10..-1] Window Streak Len Heads Ratio Alternation P(H | H) Rolling Vector Dense 1 32 Neurons ReLU Act. Dense 2 16 Neurons ReLU Act. Output σ(z3) Sigmoid ∈ (0,1) τ = 0.50 Threshold ≥ 0.5: HEADS < 0.5: TAILS The Motivation & Physical Dynamics While fine-tuning massive generative models like ACE-Step with LoRA adapts pre-existing representations, building a deep neural network from scratch exercises the fundamental physics of machine learning: feature engineering, loss gradient propagation, activation non-linearities, and generalization boundaries. I designed and trained an end-to-end binary sequence classifier on CPU using PyTorch 2.13 to explore whether a neural network could discover patterns in sequential Bernoulli events such as coin flips. In pure probability theory, an ideal memoryless coin has maximum Shannon entropy ( H = 1.0 bit ) and an insurmountable 50.0% predictive ceiling. However, empirical physical processes and human decision-makers are not memoryless. Human coin tossers exhibit pronounced Alternation Bias and Gambler’s Fallacy (excessive switching after streaks), while mechanical tosses precess in 3D flight—a phenomenon proven by Stanford mathematicians Persi Diaconis, Susan Holmes, and Richard Montgomery, where tumbling coins land on their starting face roughly 51%–53% of the time. 📊 Statistical Diagnostics & Holdout Confusion Matrix 1,200 Holdout Test Samples • Authoritative 120-Epoch CPU Verification Suite Fixed Benchmark Data Confusion Matrix (1,200 Holdout Samples) Pred. Heads Pred. Tails Act. Heads 361 True Positive (TP) Hit! (Called Heads & was Heads) 247 False Negative (FN) Miss! (Called Tails, was Heads) Act. Tails 322 False Positive (FP) False Alarm! (Called Heads, was Tails) 270 True Negative (TN) Clear! (Called Tails & was Tails) Precision (The “Wolf Cry / Trust” Score) 52.86% Recall / Sensitivity (The “Safety Net / Catch” Score) 59.38% Specificity (The “Calm Guard Dog” Score) 45.61% F1-Score (The Balanced Gold Standard) 55.93% Matthews Correlation (MCC) (The “No-Cheating” Report Card) +0.0503 Noise Perturbation & Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) Synthetic label corruption simulates noisy sensor readings and accidental bit-flips to measure how gracefully the model resists background interference. Noise Injected SNR (dB) Accuracy BCE Loss Edge vs. 50% 0% (Pure Clean) 99.9 dB 52.58% 0.7035 +2.58% 5% (Low Static) 12.8 dB 51.42% 0.7126 +1.42% 10% (Moderate Fuzz) 9.5 dB 52.25% 0.7117 +2.25% 15% (Heavy Static) 7.5 dB 51.75% 0.7151 +1.75% 20% (High Distort) 6.0 dB 51.83% 0.7216 +1.83% 30% (Extreme Noise) 3.7 dB 52.00% 0.7425 +2.00% 50% (White Noise) 0.0 dB 48.83% 0.7502 -1.17% Key Observation: The neural network maintains a positive predictive edge up to 30% sequence corruption, only dropping below 50% when exposed to 50% pure white noise ($SNR = 0.0 ext{ dB}$). 💡 Real-World Analogy Guide: Plain-English Translations 1. Confusion Matrix → Factory Quality Control Tally Think of an automated optical scanner inspecting smartphones on an assembly line: True Positives are real defective screens caught before shipping; True Negatives are flawless phones passed to packaging; False Positives are perfect phones flagged because of a harmless speck of dust; False Negatives are loose buttons that accidentally slipped through. 2. F1-Score → The Two-Way Athlete Like evaluating an NBA basketball player: if a player only shoots one single layup all year and makes it, their shooting accuracy is 100%, but they're useless to the team! The F1-score prevents the AI from cheating by balancing aggressive catching (Recall) with cautious accuracy (Precision). 3. Shannon Entropy → Sahara vs. Michigan Weather Forecasting tomorrow's weather in the Sahara desert has 0 surprise (0.0 bits). But predicting spring weather in Michigan has high chaos and high surprise (~1.0 bit). High entropy means the coin sequence is wild noise; low entropy means there is a clear, predictable pattern. 4. SNR → Car Radio in a Tunnel Like driving into a highway tunnel while listening to FM radio: as static creeps in, you can still hear the melody until the static drowns out the music (0 dB). This sweep proves the AI detects the pattern even through 20% static. Technical Implementation Feature Representation (14 Dimensions): Evaluates a sliding window of the last 10 binary outcomes alongside four higher-order statistical dynamics: normalized streak magnitude, rolling heads ratio, first-order alternation frequency, and empirical transition probabilities P(H | H) . Model Architecture: Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) consisting of a 14-dimensional input layer, Dense(32) with ReLU activation, Dense(16) with ReLU activation, and a single Sigmoid output unit (ŷ ∈ (0, 1)) parameterized by 1,025 trainable weights and biases. CPU Optimization & 120-Epoch Loss: Trained across 120 extended epochs strictly on CPU using PyTorch 2.13 with Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) loss and the Adam optimizer with Cosine Annealing learning rate decay (α = 0.005 → 0.0005, weight decay 10 -4 ). Training loss dropped monotonically from 0.6898 down to a verified record of 0.6301 , driving holdout accuracy to 63.94% and holdout F1-score to 55.93% (+5.93% above theoretical 50/50 baseline). Zero-Dependency Client-Side Engine & Human vs. AI Challenge: Exported the 1,025 fixed benchmark weights into a zero-dependency vanilla JavaScript tensor engine ( ai-predictor.html ). Visitors can test their intuition against the 120-epoch PyTorch AI in an interactive mini-game (Best of 5, 10, 20, or Endless), inspect the live Neural Mind Stream HUD streaming cognitive deductions in real time, and verify rolling prediction tapes with zero visitor CPU retraining load. title: Interactive Polyglot Code Runner & Plain-English Error Coach: Zero-Download In-Browser Execution & Isolated Host Sandbox
snippet: Interactive Polyglot Code Runner & Plain-English Error Coach: Zero-Download In-Browser Execution & Isolated Host Sandbox Live Production Interactive WebAssembly Suite & MFA-Guarded Host Compiler A zero-download, in-browser code execution playground and intelli...
content: Interactive Polyglot Code Runner & Plain-English Error Coach: Zero-Download In-Browser Execution & Isolated Host Sandbox Live Production Interactive WebAssembly Suite & MFA-Guarded Host Compiler A zero-download, in-browser code execution playground and intelligent error diagnostic coach designed to solve a ubiquitous barrier in software engineering education: the overhead of installing compilers, runtime environments, package managers, and toolchains just to experiment with a code snippet or understand an algorithmic concept. Deployed directly within this portfolio ( code-runner.html ), visitors can write, execute, inspect, and debug code across eight diverse languages and paradigms with zero local setup. 100% In-Browser Tier 1 WASM / Web Worker isolation 8 Languages Python, JS, SQL, x86, C, C++, Java, C# TOTP MFA Guarded Zero NUC load · Isolated Linux HP host Plain-English Coach Rookie trap detection & copy-paste fixes Multi-Tier Execution Architecture & Sandboxing Tier 1: Client-Side WebAssembly & Web Workers (Zero Server Load): Python 3.12: Bootstrapped through Pyodide (WASM CPython 3.12 compilation) with virtualized standard library execution and real-time stdout / stderr stream redirection. JavaScript: Evaluated inside an isolated Web Worker sandbox with strict execution time guards and custom console.log intercepts. SQL & Relational Persistence: Full SQLite relational database engine compiled to WASM via sql.js . Queries persist client-side within browser sessionStorage across page navigations, complete with visual table rendering, column headers, and a one-click Reset Sample Database action. x86 / 8086 Assembly CPU Simulator: Custom-built 32-bit register simulator featuring a live animated register bank ( EAX , EBX , ECX , EDX , ESI , EDI , ESP , EIP , and status flags ZF , CF , SF ), instruction stepping, memory inspections, and real-time operand state changes. C Simulation: Zero-dependency ANSI C pre-compilation parser executing formatted printf , variable scopes, mathematical calculations, and standard loops entirely in-memory. Tier 2: Native Host Sandboxing & NUC Decoupling: To protect the primary production Alpine NUC (which hosts Samba file shares, Tailscale routing, and site ingress), untrusted compilation for resource-heavy compiled languages (Java, C++, C#) is strictly decoupled and delegated to the dedicated Linux HP workstation ( 100.110.13.11 ). The NUC acts solely as a static reverse proxy and will never execute foreign binaries. Duo Mobile TOTP Multi-Factor Authentication: Compiled backend languages require an administrator passkey. Borrowing from modern paywall UI patterns, selecting Java, C++, or C# presents an elegant, dismissible MFA overlay requiring Andrew's 6-digit Duo Mobile Authenticator code. Visitors can freely cancel or click “Return to In-Browser Mode” at any time to immediately continue experimenting with Tier 1 languages without friction. Plain-English Error Coach: Rather than dumping cryptic compiler stack traces or unhelpful hex fault codes, an integrated cognitive diagnostics engine intercepts runtime exceptions and parses common beginner traps (such as missing colons in Python, forgotten semicolons in C/C++/Java, NullPointerException , array index out of bounds, Segmentation fault (core dumped) , and missing SQL tables). It outputs a three-part diagnostic breakdown: the raw system error, a plain-English explanation of why the machine was confused, and a concrete copy-paste code snippet showing how to resolve it. title: Custom Domain Email: Comparing Hosted Inbox & Forwarding Options
snippet: Custom Domain Email: Comparing Hosted Inbox & Forwarding Options In Progress Researching options and planning the setup I am exploring a custom email address for my portfolio's domain and comparing ways to manage incoming and outgoing mail. The project is curr...
content: Custom Domain Email: Comparing Hosted Inbox & Forwarding Options In Progress Researching options and planning the setup I am exploring a custom email address for my portfolio's domain and comparing ways to manage incoming and outgoing mail. The project is currently in the research and planning stage; I have not selected a provider or completed a live setup. I am considering a managed inbox through services such as Zoho Mail, iCloud+ Custom Email Domain, Google Workspace, or Fastmail, as well as Cloudflare Email Routing with a separate sending service. I am comparing how each approach fits my existing inbox, preferred email apps, budget, and maintenance needs. I am also planning the domain's DNS configuration: MX records for incoming mail, SPF and DKIM for authorized and signed outgoing messages, and a DMARC policy for domain authentication. Next steps are to choose an approach, configure the required records, and test sending and receiving before using the address publicly.

title: Gmail Spam Cleanup with Google Apps Script
snippet: Gmail Spam Cleanup with Google Apps Script Personal Automation Scheduled every 30 minutes I like keeping a neat inbox and creating email rules to organize incoming messages. I worked with AI to build this small Google Apps Script, which retrieves threads alrea...
content: Gmail Spam Cleanup with Google Apps Script Personal Automation Scheduled every 30 minutes I like keeping a neat inbox and creating email rules to organize incoming messages. I worked with AI to build this small Google Apps Script, which retrieves threads already in Gmail's Spam folder and moves them to Trash. It does not decide which messages are spam or immediately delete them permanently. A time-driven trigger runs emptySpamFolder every 30 minutes. I checked both the script and its trigger settings to document the actual behavior and schedule. function emptySpamFolder() { var threads = GmailApp.getSpamThreads(); for (var i = 0; i < threads.length; i++) { GmailApp.moveThreadToTrash(threads[i]); } }

title: GLPI: Personal Computer & Software Inventory
snippet: GLPI: Personal Computer & Software Inventory In Progress Dashboard live; eight computers reporting inventory; expanding the fleet I built a free inventory system for the computers I manage, inspired by the asset management tools I used during my Fishbeck inter...
content: GLPI: Personal Computer & Software Inventory In Progress Dashboard live; eight computers reporting inventory; expanding the fleet I built a free inventory system for the computers I manage, inspired by the asset management tools I used during my Fishbeck internship. Tailscale helps me connect to my machines and see when they were last online; GLPI adds a central view of their operating systems, hardware, and installed software. I worked with AI to deploy GLPI 12 and a MariaDB database in Docker on my always-on Alpine Linux Intel NUC. The database and application files live on persistent storage, and the containers are configured to restart at boot. I can open the management page from a browser on my laptop or phone through private Tailscale HTTPS. Inventory uploads use a separate authentication credential, and a daily backup job saves the database, application files, and deployment configuration. I verified the first backup completed. Eight computers are now reporting: my Linux Mint laptop, Alpine NUC, Debian-based Slax computer, Debian Mac, Kali Linux virtual machine, macOS virtual machine, Windows computer, and Windows 11 virtual machine. The enrolled computers have reported more than 11,000 software installation entries in total. I configured the agents as startup services so they can keep reporting after reboot. The different platforms needed different approaches. On Alpine, I installed the official GLPI Agent source release with native Perl dependencies and an OpenRC service so it inventories the host's APK packages. Slax runs from a USB drive, so I checked that its boot menu resumes the configured persistent session and flushed the installation and configuration changes to the USB. Windows also took file-permission troubleshooting. I had to take ownership of the files copied over SSH with my Windows administrator account and adjust access for the Windows system account, NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. I worked through the different SSH key locations for standard users and administrators, corrected the key-file permissions, and completed the inventory-agent installation with administrator elevation. I then checked that Windows had uploaded its hardware and software inventory successfully. My maintenance log records those permission fixes and the macOS VM's SSH setup. I am continuing the rollout to more virtual machines and my Apple Silicon Mac. This project focuses on keeping an accurate inventory; managing software updates centrally is a possible future addition.

title: Alpine Linux NUC: Remote Desktop & Docker Maintenance
snippet: Alpine Linux NUC: Remote Desktop & Docker Maintenance Completed Project Completed October 10, 2026 I worked with AI to make remote access and the development tools on my Intel NUC more reliable. My two VNC connections were supposed to show the same desktop at ...
content: Alpine Linux NUC: Remote Desktop & Docker Maintenance Completed Project Completed October 10, 2026 I worked with AI to make remote access and the development tools on my Intel NUC more reliable. My two VNC connections were supposed to show the same desktop at different sizes, but they were actually running separate desktops. Firefox was already open on one, which caused a browser-profile conflict when I tried to open it from the other. I consolidated the connections onto one shared desktop, with a smaller view that keeps the correct proportions and a larger view. After testing the smaller connection, I added 150% text scaling and enlarged the panel controls to make it easier to read. I reduced Openbox to one workspace, fixed the dock's app icons, and corrected browser launchers. I also adjusted startup settings and configured a persistent VNC certificate. Both connections now show the same windows. I also added persistent status indicators to the bottom panel: the network link, download and upload speeds when traffic is active, and hard-drive read/write activity with book and pencil icons. Network speeds use megabits per second, like Speedtest, while disk speeds use megabytes per second; the units are explained in tooltips to keep the panel compact. I installed GNOME Software with Alpine's package backend and added an update indicator that checks the host's package repositories hourly. It shows whether updates are available, everything is current, or a fresh check is needed, and opens the software centre when clicked. These settings load with the shared desktop at startup. I updated my Codex and Homebrew Docker containers, including their system packages and installed tools. I worked through an outdated repository signing key, checked for remaining updates and missing dependencies, and saved updated local images while keeping the mounted data. I also installed Antigravity CLI directly on the host and replaced an old launcher that pointed to a missing container. For a fallback if OpenSSH fails, I set up a separate Dropbear SSH server restricted to my private Tailscale network. The NUC's hard drive made the updates and image saves slow, so this took patience, persistence, and endurance. I kept checking the logs and testing the results until the remote desktop, browser launches, and updated tools were working.

title: Windows XP Remote Administration

content: Windows XP Remote Administration RDP & Audio Troubleshooting Completed SSH In Progress I established Remote Desktop access from my Mac to a Windows XP computer. I used Nmap and Netcat to check network connectivity and service ports, worked through Windows Firewall settings, and verified that the Remote Desktop service was available before connecting. After connecting, music played through my Mac instead of the speakers attached to the XP computer. I traced this to Remote Desktop audio redirection and changed the client’s audio setting to play sound on the remote PC. That kept playback on the XP computer’s own speakers. I also installed freeSSHd and verified that it was listening on TCP port 22. Remote SSH connection attempts were still blocked or filtered in my last tests, so command-line access through SSH remains unfinished.

content: Remote Windows Wake & Access Completed Project I configured my Intel NUC running Alpine Linux and connected my devices through Tailscale so I could SSH into the NUC from other networks. From there, I sent Wake-on-LAN magic packets to wake my Windows PC remotely. I adjusted the Windows PC’s Ethernet adapter settings in Device Manager to support waking over the network and configured automatic sleep so the computer could return to a low-power state after use. This gave me a way to wake the PC when I needed remote access without leaving it running all the time.

title: macOS Tahoe Installer & VM Setup
snippet: macOS Tahoe Installer & VM Setup In Progress Bootable installer and VM running; SMBIOS hardware identity injected with Antigravity AI I used Codex to help build a Python workflow that turns Apple’s official macOS Tahoe installer into an ISO, a disk-image file ...
content: macOS Tahoe Installer & VM Setup In Progress Bootable installer and VM running; SMBIOS hardware identity injected with Antigravity AI I used Codex to help build a Python workflow that turns Apple’s official macOS Tahoe installer into an ISO, a disk-image file that a virtual machine can boot from. I worked through installer verification errors and limited disk space, then used Apple’s tools to create and convert the bootable installer. The ISO successfully booted in the virtual machine on my Windows PC, where Tahoe is now running. I also created two snapshots so I could return to an earlier state while testing. The VM now also has passwordless SSH, administrator access for maintenance, and a GLPI inventory agent configured to start at boot. Its first hardware and software inventory reached the dashboard successfully. To resolve the Apple Account sign-in failure in System Settings, I investigated the underlying authentication logs with Antigravity AI. Apple's authentication servers ( gsa.apple.com ) strictly enforce hardware attestation through DeviceCheck BAA and AuthKit Anisette data. Because the virtual machine broadcast generic VMware virtual hardware identifiers (model VMware20,1 , a dummy serial starting with VM , and default virtual ROM strings), device provisioning was rejected with AKAnisetteError -8008 and com.apple.devicecheck.error.baa -10000 . Working in pair programming with Antigravity AI , we located previously generated valid Apple SMBIOS hardware identifiers matching an 11th Gen Intel iMac20,1 profile (Board ID Mac-CFF7D910A743CAAF , Serial Number C02CTGYGPN5T , Board Serial / MLB C02023207J9PHC11F , ROM AC293ADFC830 , and SmUUID D75E9BA5-B35B-4A6D-A72D-4F419102AD48 ). Antigravity AI backed up the virtual machine configuration ( macOS 26.vmx.bak ) and injected the complete SMBIOS parameter block into macOS 26.vmx , setting host reflection flags to FALSE so the VM presents authentic Apple hardware identities to the operating system. Next steps are booting the VM, resetting cached authentication daemons ( killall -9 akd accountsd ), and verifying Apple Account sign-in.

title: Slax Debian Persistence Repair & Automated System Upgrade
snippet: Slax Debian Persistence Repair & Automated System Upgrade Completed Project Slax Linux · Debian 12 Bookworm · QEMU WHPX Emulation · Initramfs Rootcopy Hooks · Completed November 13, 2026 How pair programming with Google DeepMind's Antigravity AI diagnosed an i...
content: Slax Debian Persistence Repair & Automated System Upgrade Completed Project Slax Linux · Debian 12 Bookworm · QEMU WHPX Emulation · Initramfs Rootcopy Hooks · Completed November 13, 2026 How pair programming with Google DeepMind's Antigravity AI diagnosed an interrupted DPKG upgrade, restored broken MagicDNS lookups via early-boot initramfs hooks, and resolved Windows Hypervisor Platform (WHPX) APIC interrupt collisions to achieve seamless bare-metal persistence. Successfully completed and finalized the persistent Slax Debian environment. After a background package upgrade was abruptly interrupted by a forced hardware power-off—leaving DPKG in a broken locked state, crashing the Fluxbox/Xorg desktop session, and disabling network name resolution—I collaborated with Antigravity AI to develop an automated in-situ repair and maintenance framework. Interrupted DPKG & DNS Lockout → Initramfs Rootcopy Early Hook Injection → QEMU WHPX User-APIC Virtualization → Clean Bare-Metal Persistence Sync Early-Boot Rootcopy Hook & Package State Recovery We engineered an early-boot hook within the USB drive's /slax/rootcopy/ directory that executes directly from initramfs before the root filesystem switch. The hook automatically resets package manager locks, injects persistent public DNS fallbacks ( 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 ) to bypass Tailscale overlay drops, repairs corrupted package dependencies with apt-get --fix-broken install , and runs a complete distribution upgrade ( apt-get dist-upgrade ). Virtualizing Bare-Metal Drives with QEMU & WHPX To safely test and execute this upgrade directly on Windows without cycling physical machines, we resolved a Windows Hypervisor Platform (WHPX) APIC interrupt conflict ( exit code 4 ) by reconfiguring QEMU with userspace interrupt emulation ( -machine pc,accel=whpx,kernel-irqchip=off ) and host CPU instruction passthrough. Following full system verification and clean buffer synchronization, the USB storage was safely dismounted and ejected via Win32 storage control calls. AI collaboration credit: In pair programming with Antigravity AI, diagnosed the DPKG frontend lock, engineered the initramfs hook, resolved the WHPX APIC conflict, and verified the bare-metal persistence architecture. title: Persistent Network Storage on My Intel NUC
snippet: Persistent Network Storage on My Intel NUC Completed Project I set up a USB drive on my Intel NUC as shared network storage that I can access from both Windows and Mac. The NUC runs Alpine Linux and uses Samba, software that lets Linux provide a shared drive t...
content: Persistent Network Storage on My Intel NUC Completed Project I set up a USB drive on my Intel NUC as shared network storage that I can access from both Windows and Mac. The NUC runs Alpine Linux and uses Samba, software that lets Linux provide a shared drive to other computers. I worked through the drive mounting, login permissions, and automatic startup so the storage stays available without rebuilding the setup each time the NUC restarts. The drive mounts automatically, and Samba and Tailscale start with the server. Tailscale connects my computers through a private network, so I can reach the same shared storage remotely as well. The result is one persistent place for my files that I can connect to from Windows or macOS, including when I am away from the NUC.

title: Private Local-AI Portfolio Assistant
snippet: Private Local-AI Portfolio Assistant Dynamic Local Answers Updated October 15, 2026 I built the chatbot in the corner of this website to answer questions about my experience, skills, and projects. It now runs NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano 4B locally on my Windows PC ...
content: Private Local-AI Portfolio Assistant Dynamic Local Answers Updated October 15, 2026 I built the chatbot in the corner of this website to answer questions about my experience, skills, and projects. It now runs NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano 4B locally on my Windows PC through LM Studio. Visitor messages pass through my Alpine Linux Intel NUC and a private SSH connection over Tailscale. The website assistant has no cloud fallback and no tools to read files, run commands, download videos, or control devices. The project evolved from getting the model connection and startup recovery working to testing what visitors could make it say. Earlier tests showed that a system prompt alone did not reliably keep the model on topic, so I initially restricted it to selecting a prewritten portfolio answer. I replaced that answer-selection flow with dynamic generation. The gateway retrieves relevant curated portfolio notes and sends them to Nemotron with the visitor's question. The model writes a fresh answer tailored to the question, with instructions to use those notes, acknowledge missing information, and stay focused on my documented work. These are generated explanations rather than a menu of stored replies; grounding reduces unsupported claims but does not guarantee perfect factuality. The gateway retains five requests per rolling minute per visitor IP, request and answer size limits, one website inference at a time, and screening for unrelated or instruction-changing requests. Client-supplied conversation history is rejected, so each question should stand on its own. Private, rotated prompt logs use pseudonymous client identifiers and redact common credential patterns; the chat interface discloses logging. I tested distinct generated answers to portfolio questions and checked that unrelated and instruction-changing requests were refused. The separate phone assistant shares the same Windows model but has its own general-purpose prompt and spoken-response pipeline. Both request a thirty-minute idle unload timer; the gateway allows additional time for loading and generation. I will continue checking answer quality and portfolio coverage as projects change. title: Sudoku Vision & Cognitive Reasoning Engine
snippet: Sudoku Vision & Cognitive Reasoning Engine Live & Interactive Computer Vision · Heuristic Deduction · Zero-Idle Architecture · October 23, 2026 The Concept Inspired by interactive browser-based portfolio demos, I wanted to showcase an active, visible problem-s...
content: Sudoku Vision & Cognitive Reasoning Engine Live & Interactive Computer Vision · Heuristic Deduction · Zero-Idle Architecture · October 23, 2026 The Concept Inspired by interactive browser-based portfolio demos, I wanted to showcase an active, visible problem-solving task operating client-side in the browser. With assistance from Antigravity CLI, I designed and engineered an event-driven computer vision and cognitive reasoning pipeline. While game bots like Connect 4 are typically driven by canned minimax tree searches, Sudoku provides a compelling stage for true cognitive reasoning: constraint propagation, candidate elimination, pedagogical rule explanation, and search-tree backtracking. What Got Built Optical Scan & Grid Ingestion: A client-side drag-and-drop upload zone that accepts photos and screenshots of Sudoku puzzles (from morning newspapers, paperback puzzle books, or mobile screens) and renders an optical alignment grid overlay onto HTML5 Canvas. Includes four authentic pre-rendered styles (Newspaper, Modern Mobile App, Puzzle Book, and Diabolical Escargot). Interactive 9×9 Digital Verification Grid: A responsive, keyboard-navigable 9×9 board with 3×3 box demarcations, arrow-key navigation, candidate pencil marking, and manual digit override before initiating solving. Pedagogical Cognitive Engine: A human-like deduction engine that evaluates candidate numbers (1–9) per cell, prioritizes deterministic logical rules (Sole Candidates and Hidden Candidates across rows, columns, and 3×3 boxes), and falls back to Minimum Remaining Values (MRV) heuristic branching when pure deduction is exhausted. Live Cognitive Thought Stream: A dark terminal-style telemetry panel streaming Nemo’s natural-language deductions in real time, with color-coded classification tags ( SOLE CANDIDATE , HIDDEN CANDIDATE , BRANCH CHOICE , BACKTRACK ), real-time deduction/backtrack counters, remaining cell tallies, and variable execution speeds ranging from pedagogical slow-step up to Turbo. Zero-Idle Compute Architecture: Because Sudoku extraction and heuristic solving are purely event-driven, the engine operates client-side with zero continuous GPU VRAM or CPU overhead on the backend infrastructure when idle. title: Mind Reader AI: In-Browser Human Randomness & Choice Predictor
snippet: Mind Reader AI: In-Browser Human Randomness & Choice Predictor In Active Development Custom ML Architecture · ONNX Web · Shannon Entropy Telemetry · Launching Tomorrow · October 24, 2026 The Concept Humans are notoriously incapable of producing true mathematic...
content: Mind Reader AI: In-Browser Human Randomness & Choice Predictor In Active Development Custom ML Architecture · ONNX Web · Shannon Entropy Telemetry · Launching Tomorrow · October 24, 2026 The Concept Humans are notoriously incapable of producing true mathematical randomness. When asked to simulate a random sequence of coin flips (Heads vs. Tails) or rapid keystrokes, cognitive biases—such as alternation bias (over-switching between choices), clustering aversion (avoiding long streaks), and subconscious rhythmic cadences—leave distinct probabilistic fingerprints. Collaborating with Antigravity CLI , I am engineering a real-time machine learning prediction engine (“Mind Reader”) that analyzes human input patterns on the fly to predict the visitor's next choice with statistically significant advantage over 50/50 baseline chance. Architecture & Technical Specifications To ensure high throughput and zero latency without exposing backend infrastructure to compute exhaustion, the engine executes entirely within the visitor’s web browser. It combines higher-order Markov transition matrices with a compact neural sequence classifier exported directly to ONNX Web format. Component Implementation Spec Performance Metric / Target Inference Runtime ONNX Runtime Web (Wasm / SIMD edge execution) < 3.5 ms per choice (zero network hops) Model Architecture Higher-Order Markov (k=3 to 5) + Bi-LSTM / FFNN Sequence Head Target 68%–78% accuracy vs. humans (50% chance) Information Theory Real-time Shannon Entropy: H(X) = -Σ P(x) log2 P(x) Quantifies non-randomness deviation from 1.000 bit Visual Telemetry Running Loss Curve, Confusion Matrix, and Confidence Bar Dual-axis Loss vs. Rounds vector graph Server Resource Cost Zero-Idle / Client-Side WebAssembly sandbox 0 MB Server VRAM • 0% Host CPU Utilization Development is actively underway with Antigravity CLI. A dedicated interactive demonstration page with real-time prediction gameplay, running loss graphs, and interactive telemetry dials will deploy tomorrow.

title: Phone AI Gateway: PIN-Free PSTN Bridge, Liquid LFM-2.5 & Real-Time Voice Cloning
snippet: Phone AI Gateway: PIN-Free PSTN Bridge, Liquid LFM-2.5 & Real-Time Voice Cloning Live Prototype Hotline Twilio PSTN Gateway · Liquid LFM-2.5 1.2B · Coqui XTTS-v2 Voice Cloning · Async GPU Pre-Warming · Updated November 16, 2026 Interactive Telephone Hotline De...
content: Phone AI Gateway: PIN-Free PSTN Bridge, Liquid LFM-2.5 & Real-Time Voice Cloning Live Prototype Hotline Twilio PSTN Gateway · Liquid LFM-2.5 1.2B · Coqui XTTS-v2 Voice Cloning · Async GPU Pre-Warming · Updated November 16, 2026 Interactive Telephone Hotline Demo 📞 +1 (912) 915-3851 Call from any phone to converse aloud with local Liquid LFM-2.5 • Voice Clone: Real-time XTTS-v2 synthesis matching Andrew's voice • Guardrails: 5-minute limit • 1 call per 15 min • Zero-silence hold music. Call Hotline → I built a dedicated personal telephone gateway that connects real cellular and landline telephone calls directly to local artificial intelligence models running inside my homelab. Originally conceived as a multi-tier menu requiring PIN authentication to route calls to either Google Gemini or local models on a Linux HP computer, I streamlined the entire architecture into an instant-access, PIN-free voice bridge that connects inbound callers directly to local neural models running on my NVIDIA RTX A2000 Laptop GPU. Multi-Node Telephony & Voice Synthesis Topology The operational pipeline bridges public telephone networks to local private infrastructure across three nodes: Inbound PSTN Ingestion (Twilio Voice Webhook): Inbound calls to +1 (912) 915-3851 are routed via HTTP POST webhooks to a secure public endpoint published through Tailscale Funnel. Telephony Gateway Controller (Alpine Linux Intel NUC): Hosted on my Alpine Linux gateway ( 100.87.81.52 ), an asynchronous FastAPI service ( servingcall.py ) validates Twilio cryptographic signatures, manages session tokens, enforces caller frequency cooldowns (15 minutes per caller ID), tracks 5-minute hard call duration limits, and directs Twilio TwiML execution loops. Dual-Channel Port Forwarding (Tailscale SSH Tunnels): The NUC maintains persistent reverse SSH tunnels to the Windows gaming PC ( model-pc ), forwarding port 12340 to LM Studio (port 1234 ) for text inference and port 8020 to a dedicated Coqui XTTS-v2 microservice for voice synthesis. Model Evolution to Liquid LFM-2.5 1.2B: After testing larger models that suffered under background distributed compute (Folding@Home), I standardized the language engine on Liquid AI's Liquid Foundation Model ( liquid/lfm2.5-1.2b ). LFM-2.5 consistently delivers sub-1.5 second inference latencies (~1,465 ms) on the 4 GB RTX A2000 Laptop GPU even while FahCore_28 executes at 95% GPU load. Conditioned Voice Cloning (Coqui XTTS-v2): Rather than relying on generic synthetic text-to-speech, callers who dial in hear responses synthesized directly in my own voice. The Windows microservice uses Coqui XTTS-v2 conditioned on a reference voice sample ( voice_sample.wav ) stored on the host. Whitelisted personal numbers bypass synthesis to receive instantaneous Twilio <Say> prompts, while public and non-whitelisted callers receive custom cloned audio served dynamically via /audio/{job_id}.wav . Field Troubleshooting: Resolving the Voice Fallback Deadlock & Hold Music Silence During live testing from external numbers (including Google Voice), I observed two critical UX bugs: callers heard Twilio's default robotic text-to-speech voice instead of my voice clone, and the elevator hold music abruptly cut out into awkward dead silence after only two seconds while waiting for the model to reply. In pair programming with Antigravity AI , we diagnosed and remediated both issues: Diagnosing the Cold-Start Voice Fallback Deadlock: Inspecting gateway.log revealed that every non-whitelisted call logged [TTS-INFO] TTS model not resident in VRAM; using instant voice fallback . A previous memory optimization had configured a 60-second idle auto-unload timer in server.py to free VRAM, while a safety check in servingcall.py inspected /health and immediately aborted synthesis whenever model_loaded was false. Because the service automatically purged GPU weights after 60 seconds of inactivity, 100% of inbound calls found the model cold, skipped synthesis, and fell back to Twilio's default voice. The model was never called and could never load naturally. Asynchronous Pre-Warming & Resident Cache Architecture: To eliminate cold-start latency without blocking the caller, we added an asynchronous /warmup endpoint to the Windows TTS microservice and connected it to POST /call on the NUC. The exact millisecond an inbound call connects, the gateway dispatches a background warmup trigger. While the caller listens to the initial greeting (“Liquid is ready...”) and speaks their question (~20–25 seconds total), XTTS-v2 loads its weights into GPU VRAM in parallel. By the time LLM inference finishes, XTTS-v2 is hot and synthesizes speech in 4.0–4.6 seconds. We restored the auto-unload timer to 30 minutes (1800s) and added post-synthesis torch.cuda.empty_cache() , keeping resident VRAM steady at ~1.8 GB and leaving >2.2 GB free for LM Studio and Folding@Home. Eliminating Dead Silence in the Hold Music Loop: We investigated why hold music cut out after two seconds. The original audio loop ( hold_loop.mp3 ) was only 2.5 seconds long, but Twilio's <Gather> verb defaulted to a 5.0-second silence timeout waiting for DTMF keypresses. Consequently, callers experienced 2.5 seconds of music followed by 5.0 seconds of dead silence on every cycle. We re-encoded Kevin MacLeod's “Local Forecast - Elevator” into an 8.0-second seamless loop with 0.2s smooth volume fades, and configured <Gather num_digits=2 timeout=0> . Twilio now streams continuous, unbroken hold music that immediately hands off to the cloned voice the moment synthesis finishes. AI collaboration credit: Andrew Van Ek supplied personal voice calibration data ( voice_sample.wav ), conducted live PSTN telephony verification across Google Voice and cellular networks, reported the default voice fallback and hold audio stutter, and conceived the pre-warming architecture. Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) analyzed gateway logs over SSH, isolated the 60-second auto-unload / circuit-breaker deadlock, engineered the asynchronous /warmup background pre-loader on Windows port 8020, extended the resident idle cache to 30 minutes, re-encoded the 8.0-second seamless hold music loop, configured zero-silence Twilio TwiML gathering, verified the end-to-end pipeline, and authored this documentation.
