Heyboer Created • 100% MD5 Checksum Match • 8 Notebook & Rescue Moved • Flip Phone Dumps to Backups Staging Deleted • Verified Project Overview & Incident Evolution What originated as a hardware-level data disaster recovery project on a friend’s failing physical magnetic hard drive evolved into a real-time, cross-network forensic audit and multi-tier cryptographic deduplication operation. Working alongside Antigravity AI (Google DeepMind agentic assistant) over an active workstation session, we transformed what was expected to be an unassisted overnight storage crawl into a 15.4-second parallel SQLite indexing run , proved complete bitstream parity across 23+ GB of nested archive payloads, migrated all recovered assets into a clean sequential namespace on my primary network storage array ( ONEFIVE , drive B:\ ), and verified 100% cryptographic integrity before safely pruning redundant local staging storage. Phase 1: Physical Drive Disaster Recovery & ddrescue Sector Carving In September 2026, a physical hard drive suffered severe magnetic platter degradation and mounting I/O read timeouts. Rather than executing unstable filesystem-level copy operations that risk catastrophic drive head crashes, I established an isolated, forensic disk-imaging pipeline: FTK Imager Bitstream Acquisition: Extracted raw sector data into an uncompressed image, carefully cataloging sector read anomalies and logging areas where the software wrote deterministic zero-fills rather than falsifying data. Targeted GNU ddrescue Phase Retries: Isolated the damaged logical sectors and deployed GNU ddrescue across multiple strategic retries (generating detailed domain logfiles sector-26091312.map and carved chunks sector-26091312.bin for retries v1, v2, and v3). Four persistent bad sectors were isolated; by strictly documenting unreadable blocks rather than claiming complete recovery, data provenance was maintained with complete forensic transparency. Monolithic Image Packaging: Reconstructed the salvageable NTFS partition structure into a unified 23.12 GB (23,122,215,753-byte) compressed master archive titled HeyboerFULLDownloadHere.zip , preserving 5,071 carved files across user directories ( AppData/ , Fun/ , Pictures/ , Public/ , and the recovery telemetry directory Tried Rescuing/ ). Phase 2: The Staging Dilemma & The "Overnight" Search Assumption By late November 2026, the 23.12 GB master archive sat staged in a local workstation download directory ( C:\Users\Owner\Downloads\EventuallyShipToOneFive ) alongside several other unorganized payloads: Public.zip (480.8 MB), Tried Rescuing.zip (3.3 KB), 8 Notebook.zip (65.8 MB), a Google Takeout export of vintage Cydia iOS jailbreak repository PDF documentation, and raw diagnostic phone dumps from an LG Accolade (VX5600) CDMA flip phone. Before purging the staging folder or transferring files across the network, the crucial question was: What, if any, of this data has already been copied to the primary network storage drive ( ONEFIVE / drive B:\ via Tailscale SMB)? Sub-Minute Indexing Record: Indexed the entire 375.37 GB volume—cataloging all 62,651 files across 2,454 directories—in exactly 15.4 seconds . Targeted Indexed Queries: With indexed columns on (name_lower, size) , queries that typically require recursive filesystem walks resolved in under 2 milliseconds. We proved that 100% of both archives' payloads (including all 4,302 documents in Public/Documents/ and all ddrescue sector maps) existed identically inside HeyboerFULLDownloadHere.zip with matching CRC32 checksums and file lengths . Prior Phone & Audio Verifications: All 121 ringtones in VX5600-Accolade-Ringtones were bit-for-bit identical to B:\05. Backups\FlipPhoneStuff\05. LG Flip Phone Stuff\VX5600-Accolade.zip , and all 4 Cydia PDF documents were already stored in B:\26. iPod Touch Stuff\ . Phase 5: Homelab Migration, Bitstream Parity & Safe Pruning With exact overlap mapped, we executed a clean, structured migration plan: Sequential Namespace Preservation ( B:\28. Heyboer ): To prevent collision with 23. driveRootFilez and continue the sequential numbering beyond 27. iPAs , created a permanent home at B:\28. Heyboer . Backups\FlipPhoneStuff\05. LG Flip Phone Stuff\ . title: Troubleshooting an FTK Imager Crash
snippet: Troubleshooting an FTK Imager Crash Troubleshooting Case Study Documented September 21, 2026 I investigated an FTK Imager crash that happened repeatedly when I selected a small FAT32 USB drive. Windows could browse the drive normally, and its disk check report...
content: Troubleshooting an FTK Imager Crash Troubleshooting Case Study Documented September 21, 2026 I investigated an FTK Imager crash that happened repeatedly when I selected a small FAT32 USB drive. Windows could browse the drive normally, and its disk check reported no filesystem problems. Reinstalling FTK and resetting its settings did not fix the crash. I compared another USB device and then reformatted the test drive as exFAT, another drive format. FTK worked with exFAT. That gave me a practical workaround and pointed to a compatibility issue with this particular FAT32 drive, though it did not prove the exact cause.

The Homelab Salvage Playbook & ITAM Architecture Key technical practices and IT Asset Management protocols used to keep aging silicon running reliably 24/7 without budget or thermal degradation. 01 Phase-Change Thermal Engineering Liquid and standard silicone pastes pump out under the thermal expansion cycles of 24/7 100% compute loads. Upgrading legacy laptops (such as the 2011 Mac) with Honeywell PTM7950 phase-change pads prevents dry-out and drops sustained core temperatures by 8-12°C indefinitely. 02 Stateless & Immutable Memory Runtimes Mechanical drives and cheap consumer SSDs fail early under relentless logging. Deploying custom Slax Linux live USBs with RAM overlays (like the Dell Inspiron tower) ensures that the operating system runs purely in memory, making nodes immune to drive failures and corrupt writes. 03 Fire-Safe Battery Elimination & USB Tethering Lithium-ion pouch batteries in retired mobile devices and laptops will swell when held at 100% state-of-charge on constant AC power. Removing internal batteries and plugging devices directly into host USB lines (like the S4 Mini plugged into the 2011 Mac on the bottom shelf) guarantees safe, unmonitored homelab operations. 04 GLPI IT Asset Management (ITAM) Tracking 9 heterogeneous devices across multiple shelves requires disciplined asset lifecycle tracking. Integrating hardware specs, service dates, thermal profiles, and IP/MAC allocations into a centralized GLPI asset management schema ensures zero undocumented single-points-of-failure.

title: AI Bias & Algorithmic Fairness Audit Lab
snippet: Interactive machine learning laboratory inspecting algorithmic fairness, vector embedding debiasing, and disparate impact calibration.
content: AI Bias & Algorithmic Fairness Audit Lab. Interactive machine learning laboratory inspecting algorithmic fairness, vector embedding debiasing, and disparate impact calibration. Interactive Ethical AI & Governance Lab AI Bias & Algorithmic Fairness Audit Lab AI models don't wake up with personal opinions—they learn from the examples we feed them. If the training data is full of past hiring habits, historical imbalances, or skewed numbers, the computer treats those patterns like math rules. Hover on desktop or tap on mobile on any highlighted term to see an everyday real-world comparison that doesn't involve computer jargon. ⚖️ Four-Fifths Rule (EEOC 80%) 👁️ Blind Auditions & Debiasing 📊 The Accuracy Paradox 🛡️ Fair Representation ⚡ Pass/Fail Cutoff Tuning Module 01 Resume Screening & Word Bias Simulator Automated resume screeners look at word similarities using word maps (embeddings) . If historical hires at a company were mostly from one background, resumes with different hobbies, names, or graduation years get penalized—even when their actual skills are identical. Test how background clues change scores, and see how simple fairness fixes level the playing field. Candidate Profile Setup Candidate Background & Profile Clues: Johnathan Vance (Traditional Background) Emily Davies (Women in Tech Club President) Jamal Washington (Urban STEM Leadership Fellow) Alejandro Hernandez (First-Gen Tech Scholar) Taylor Smith (Non-Binary / Gender-Neutral Phrasing) College Graduation Year (Age Clue): 2024 (Recent Graduate · Early Career) 2016 (Mid-Level · 8 Years Experience) 2002 (Senior Engineer · 22 Years Experience) 1992 (Veteran Professional · 32 Years Experience) Work History Continuity: Continuous Employment (No gaps) 2-Year Family Caregiving / Parental Leave 3-Year Military Service Transition 18-Month Medical Leave & Recovery College / Education Background: Ivy League / Elite Private University Regional State University (e.g. Grand Valley State / GVSU) Community College → State Transfer Self-Taught / Open Source Contributor Fairness Fixes (Try turning these on!): Blind Screen: Hide names, graduation years, and school logos before the computer reads the skills Blind Audition Filter : Strip out gender and demographic stereotypes from word associations Fair Passing Rate : Ensure pass rates meet the EEOC 80% Rule How the Algorithm Grades Them Raw Model Score -- → Fairness-Fixed Score -- Raw Score (Unchecked) Score After Fairness Fixes Checking... Passing Rate Ratio (DIR) : 0.00 The 80% Rule means applicants from minority groups must pass at least 80% as often as the highest group, or the test is considered unfairly tilted. Hidden Penalties & Bonuses Caught: Module 02 AI Word Predictions & Job Stereotypes Language models predict the next word in a sentence based on millions of public articles and forum posts. If past articles usually talked about doctors as men or nurses as women, the AI repeats that exact same assumption. Pick a sentence below to see which pronoun the model expects next. Select a Job Scenario: "The doctor stepped out of the operating room and explained that..." "The nurse arrived early at the clinic and checked that..." "The Chief Executive Officer addressed the boardroom and announced that..." "The executive assistant rescheduled the calendar appointments and confirmed that..." "The software architect refactored the legacy codebase because..." ⚡ Why this happens in plain English: The AI isn't thinking for itself—it is simply playing a high-speed guessing game of 'what word usually comes next?' If the older books and websites it studied wrote 'he' after doctor and 'she' after nurse, it guesses those words every time unless engineers deliberately teach it to stay neutral. Module 03 The Accuracy Trap: Why 95% Can Still Be Completely Broken Think of a security guard watching 1,000 people enter a stadium, where only 2 people are carrying fake tickets. If the guard falls asleep and waves everyone through without checking a single ticket, they were '99.8% accurate' on paper—yet they failed at the one job they were hired to do. That's the Accuracy Trap . Group Balance in the Data: 90% Majority / 10% Minority Slide right to see what happens when one group has almost zero examples. Pass / Fail Cutoff Line : 0.50 Raise or lower the score required to pass. How to Fix It: No Fix (Standard Raw Training): The computer guesses the majority every time Extra Attention Penalty: Penalize the AI harder when it makes mistakes on rare cases SMOTE Balancing : Fill in the missing shelves with realistic sample examples 90.0% Overall Accuracy (Sounds great on paper) 98.0% Majority Catch Rate (Passes easily) 18.0% Minority Catch Rate (Completely left behind!) 0.80 Opportunity Gap (Target: under 0.05) 💡 The Big Takeaway: When an AI is tested on skewed data, a high accuracy score is often just a lazy guess. Adjusting the pass line or using SMOTE balancing forces the model to actually look at qualifications instead of taking the easy way out. Module 04 The 3 Ways Engineers Fix Algorithmic Bias You don't fix bias by hoping the computer is nice—you fix it by engineering checks before, during, and after the model makes decisions. Stage What It Means Everyday Real-World Comparison The Measurement Rule Before Training (Pre-Processing) Cleaning the data and balancing the groups before teaching the computer Making sure a cookbook has healthy recipes from all over the world instead of 50 pages of just cupcakes Passing Rate Ratio (DIR ≥ 0.80) During Training (In-Processing) Penalizing the AI whenever it relies on shortcuts like names, gender, or age Telling a music judge they get docked points if they look at who is playing instead of listening to the song Demographic Parity (≤ 0.05 gap) After Training (Post-Processing) Adjusting the pass/fail line so equally qualified people get fair results Calibrating sports tryout cutoffs so honest players aren't eliminated by bad weather on their tryout day Equal Opportunity Gap (≤ 0.05)

Telemetry & Inspection Underlying Technologies Explore Project Case Study in Projects → 3D Planetary Radar Architecture & Physical Internet Telemetry While the internet is often abstracted as an ephemeral "cloud", in physical reality over 95% of international data transit relies on dense glass fibers traversing extreme ocean trenches. This planetary radar maps the physical layer of the global web: Subsea Optical Fiber Topologies Ingests TeleGeography's geospatial datasets, rendering multi-line vector paths for over 400 active international subsea cable systems. Dashed particle shaders animate kinetic photon pulses simulating light propagation across Transatlantic, Transpacific, and Arctic seabed corridors. Coastal Landing Stations & Street View Pinpoints 1,900+ coastal cable landing stations where armored wet marine cables transition into terrestrial beach manholes. Selecting any station executes a smooth camera swoop and surfaces direct one-click links to Google Street View and Mapillary panoramas. Tier 1 Global Peering & Backhaul Maps core international Internet Exchange Points (including Equinix Ashburn, DE-CIX Frankfurt, AMS-IX Amsterdam, and LINX London), tracing high-capacity optical transit arcs between subsea landings and continental backbones.

title: About Andrew Van Ek
snippet: Background, education, computing philosophy, hands-on homelab journey, and technology stack.
content: About Andrew Van Ek. Background, education, computing philosophy, hands-on homelab journey, and technology stack. My Goal My personal goal is to help as many people as possible with their technology needs. I am passionate about the intersection of human connection and technical efficiency. My Philosophy I love solving problems—including the ones that don’t strictly "need" to be solved. My personal slogan is: “If it isn’t broke, do fix it.” I believe in continuous improvement and optimization rather than just maintenance. Persistence & Dedication I pride myself on my persistence. Whether it's staying late at work to ensure plant orders are completed or spending hours at home troubleshooting a custom operating system on an old Google Pixel, I see my projects through to the end. I’ve even reinstalled Windows multiple times just to explore different versions and find the perfect configuration. That persistence is equally visible when working with vintage hardware: rather than abandoning slow or temperamental legacy machines, I recently engineered a self-healing batch sync to migrate ~283 GB of archives across network shares to a vintage Windows XP computer with just 256 MB of RAM. Because running an Ethernet cable across the room wasn't an option, the transfer runs entirely over a vintage 802.11g Wi-Fi link. By building automated reconnect routines and delta comparisons into the pipeline, the machine chugs along through an autonomous 2.5-to-3.5-day wireless endurance trial without losing data or requiring manual intervention. My Personal Computer Fleet I maintain a fleet of seven computers across multiple eras: a vintage Windows XP workstation (256 MB RAM) dedicated to retro computing experiments and legacy network interoperability, a Dell Inspiron that I plan to run Slax Linux on, a 2011 Intel Mac running Debian, an M1 Mac running macOS 27, an HP laptop I received for free from Fishbeck, another HP laptop I received for free from a couple of friends, and an Intel NUC running Alpine Linux. On my Windows computer, I also run four virtual machines: Windows 11, macOS 26 (Tahoe), Ubuntu, and Kali Linux. Virtual machines let me try different operating systems and setups on one physical computer. Keeping this collection useful is an ongoing project. I update software, upgrade systems, maintain their configurations, and work through problems as they come up. It gives me hands-on practice caring for a mix of older and newer hardware across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Linux & Everyday Automation I enjoy tinkering with Linux, keeping older computers useful, and finding small ways to make everyday technology easier to use. My Maintenance & Experiments page records the remote-access fixes, Windows permission troubleshooting, USB setups, and local AI experiments along the way. I also love creating email rules to keep a highly organized inbox. Working with AI, I built a Google Apps Script that moves Gmail spam threads to Trash automatically every 30 minutes. The project and code snippet show how a small automation can take care of a repetitive task. Fun Facts & Everyday Organization I love finding practical tricks to keep everyday technology tidy. On my phone, I organize multiple numbers using two dedicated consolidated contacts: one contact combines 20+ two-factor verification code numbers and automated SMS shortcodes into a single message thread so one-time security codes don't clutter my texts, and another contact bundles 10+ numbers that are either spam or scams so nuisance calls and texts can be easily identified, silenced, and managed in one place. Community & Communication I enjoy using my public speaking skills to share my passions. From serving on the Student Council in Middle School to helping my grandma stop a flood of spam notifications, I am never afraid to step in and communicate technical solutions clearly and effectively. My work at the GVSU IT Service Desk has strengthened my phone communication skills, especially explaining technical issues clearly and helping callers work through troubleshooting steps. Confusion Matrix → Factory Quality Control Tally Think of an automated optical scanner inspecting smartphones on an assembly line: True Positives are real defective screens caught before shipping; True Negatives are flawless phones passed to packaging; False Positives are perfect phones flagged because of a harmless speck of dust; False Negatives are loose buttons that accidentally slipped through. 2. F1-Score → The Two-Way Athlete Like evaluating an NBA basketball player: if a player only shoots one single layup all year and makes it, their shooting accuracy is 100%, but they're useless to the team! The F1-score prevents the AI from cheating by balancing aggressive catching (Recall) with cautious accuracy (Precision). 3. Shannon Entropy → Sahara vs. Michigan Weather Forecasting tomorrow's weather in the Sahara desert has 0 surprise (0.0 bits). But predicting spring weather in Michigan has high chaos and high surprise (~1.0 bit). High entropy means the coin sequence is wild noise; low entropy means there is a clear, predictable pattern. 4. SNR → Car Radio in a Tunnel Like driving into a highway tunnel while listening to FM radio: as static creeps in, you can still hear the melody until the static drowns out the music (0 dB). This sweep proves the AI detects the pattern even through 20% static. 5. Noise Perturbation → The Turbulence Wind Tunnel Like stress-testing an aircraft wing in an extreme wind tunnel or having a quarterback practice while being tackled. It deliberately shakes the input sequence to prove the AI's pattern recognition remains steadfast even through noisy interference. 6. Empirical Win-Rate → Real-World Batting Average Like evaluating a baseball hitter by their actual regular-season hits versus theoretical predictions in batting practice. Empirical win-rate tallies the exact percentage of live coin tosses the AI successfully predicted in real matches. Mathematical Foundations & Research Context 1. The 50% Theoretical Ceiling In pure probability theory, an ideal Bernoulli trial with p = 0.50 is independent and memoryless. Its Shannon information entropy is exactly H(X) = 1.0 bit . Under pure mathematical randomness, no algorithm can achieve greater than 50% long-term predictive accuracy. 2. Human Cognitive Alternation Bias Extensive psychological research demonstrates that humans are systematically poor random number generators. Subjects exhibit severe Gambler's Fallacy : after 2 or 3 identical choices, they switch outcomes with p > 0.70 . Neural networks exploit this multi-step autocorrelation to achieve 65%–72% accuracy. 3. Diaconis Physical Precession In 2007, Stanford mathematicians Persi Diaconis, Susan Holmes, and Richard Montgomery proved that natural coin tosses precess in 3D space during flight. Due to tumbling physics, flipped coins spend more time with the starting face upward, landing on the same face roughly 51%–53% of the time.

title: Privacy Policy
snippet: Local-first data privacy, cookies policy, and zero-telemetry commitment.
content: Privacy Policy. Local-first data privacy, cookies policy, and zero-telemetry commitment. Data Ethics & Transparency Privacy Policy How this website and my homelab services handle network traffic, visitor telemetry, and AI conversations. 1. Zero Raw IP Address Storage ✓ Zero Raw IP Retention In accordance with my privacy principles, zero raw IP addresses or personally identifiable coordinates are ever logged, stored in databases, or published . When you visit the site, network edge requests pass through Cloudflare proxy nodes to protect my self-hosted homelab. The homepage displays coarse regional telemetry (such as approximate country, region, or city) purely to show aggregate global visitor trends. This data is derived dynamically on the edge without capturing or retaining your physical street address or exact location. 2. Local AI & Data Sovereignty (Nemo) My on-premise AI assistant ( Nemo ) runs locally on a dedicated NVIDIA RTX GPU host connected via a private Tailscale mesh network through an Alpine Linux Intel NUC gateway: No Third-Party Brokers: Prompts sent to Nemo are processed on my own private hardware. They are never sent to commercial data aggregators, advertising brokers, or public model training pipelines. Temporary Abuse Review: Transient rate-limiting checks (5 messages/minute) are enforced in memory to protect local hardware from automated denial-of-service loops. No Account Tracking: You do not need to sign in or provide an email to chat with Nemo. 3. Dual-Brain Cloud Assistant (Google Cloud Run) The companion assistant at AI Assistant runs on Google Cloud Run utilizing Vertex AI Agent Builder. Queries are strictly used to search my grounded knowledge repositories (649 GVSU IT service-desk articles and ~977 OneDrive CIS class documents). Zero personal search profiles are constructed from your inquiries. 4. Client-Side Browser Persistence (localStorage) To provide responsive interactive tools without server-side tracking, certain preferences and benchmarks are stored exclusively inside your own browser using standard localStorage : Page Load Speed Tachometer: Your fastest page render record (milliseconds) and personal visit counter stay strictly in your browser. Nemo Chat History: Your active conversation is retained on your device so you can navigate across portfolio pages without losing answers. You can clear this anytime by clicking the Clear button in the chat header. Weather Units: Temperature scale preferences (°F vs. °C) are remembered locally. None of this local data is ever transmitted back to an external tracking database. 5. Zero Third-Party Advertising Trackers This website contains zero marketing cookies, zero Facebook Pixels, and zero commercial tracking beacons . I do not run banner advertisements or monetize visitor data in any way. 6. Contact Information If you have any questions about this policy or would like to discuss homelab security and privacy practices, feel free to reach out directly via the Contact page or email avanek737383@gmail.com .
